title: Draft Spec: Policy Engine Extensions for Regional Failover Automation
author: Jordan Lee
text:
Context / why this exists
- We’re upgrading regional failover automation as part of Reliability Program (Q1–Q2 2026). Today, routing policy evaluation has a few gaps:
 - Non-deterministic behavior in edge cases (e.g., multiple signals firing, partial signal availability, time-window ambiguity).
 - Hard to reason about priority across trigger signals (reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity exhaustion).
 - No first-class “hold-down” / dampening in evaluation; logic is split between policy rules and external controller.
 - No consistent mechanism to enforce safety constraints per tenant/tier (max flips, blast radius caps, required approval).

Goals
- Add policy engine primitives so failover decisioning is:
 - Deterministic and auditable (same inputs => same decision; explainability built-in).
 - Compatible with ADR-042 (signal priority + corroboration) and ADR-043 (rollback + anti-flap).
 - Safe by default (rate limits, required corroboration, blast radius constraints).
- Support both:
 - “Recommend” (dry-run) mode: compute candidate flips + evidence.
 - “Enforce” mode: same evaluation but returns executable actions.

Non-goals
- Replace the automation controller. The controller still orchestrates execution, approvals, and cross-system workflow.
- Re-architect signal ingestion. We consume normalized, time-bucketed signals from Region Health + SLO toolkit.
- Build customer-facing UI here.

Terminology
- Policy: configuration describing routing behavior for a route/service/model/tier.
- Region set: primary and fallback regions eligible for this route.
- Trigger signal: normalized boolean or scalar indicating regional impairment or risk.
- Decision: computed outcome (no-op, failover, partial shift, rollback, hold).
- Action: executable change (policy flip, weight adjustment, circuit breaker mode) emitted by controller.

Inputs / data model assumptions
- Policy engine receives inputs as a single evaluation payload, including:
 - route_id (e.g., hosted.chat.completions, dedicated.pool.<pool_id>)
 - tenant_id (optional for shared Hosted; required for Dedicated)
 - tenant_tier (free/pro/enterprise/dedicated)
 - current_routing_state (primary region, weights, last_flip_at)
 - signals (per region, per signal type):
 - reachability: ok|degraded|down + confidence + last_updated
 - errors_5xx_burn: burn_rate + window + confidence
 - tail_latency_burn: burn_rate + p95/p99 deltas + confidence
 - capacity_headroom: percent + “hard gate” boolean
 - control_plane_health (optional): ok|degraded|down
 - evaluation_time (UTC epoch + monotonic sequence)
 - constraints (policy-level + tenant-level): max_flips_per_hour, min_hold_down_seconds, require_approval, blast_radius_limit

Determinism requirements (core)
1) Stable ordering
- Evaluation must not depend on map iteration order.
- Rule matching must define explicit ordering: by priority, then by tie-breakers.

2) Stable time semantics
- All windowed signals must be anchored to evaluation_time and include:
 - effective_start, effective_end, and a “freshness” timestamp.
- Engine must treat stale signals consistently:
 - If authoritative signals are stale beyond threshold, decision = HOLD (do not fail over) unless reachability is explicitly DOWN with high confidence.

3) Single decision per evaluation
- For a given (route_id, tenant_id, evaluation_time), engine emits exactly one decision object, even if multiple actions are possible.
- Multi-step actions (e.g., drain -> shift weights -> finalize) must be represented as a sequence recommendation but still within a single decision record.

4) Explainability
- Decision must include:
 - decision_type (NO_OP | FAILOVER | PARTIAL_SHIFT | ROLLBACK | HOLD)
 - chosen_reason (canonical enum)
 - evidence: ordered list of signals used, with values, freshness, and thresholds.
 - rejected_candidates: (optional) top 1–3 alternatives and why they were not selected.

Proposed changes to policy engine
A) New predicates / functions
1) region_health(region, signal_type) -> {status, value, confidence, freshness_seconds}
- Wrapper that pulls normalized data from payload and enforces freshness calculations.

2) is_authoritative_reachability_down(region) -> bool
- True only if:
 - reachability.status == down
 - confidence >= configured_min_confidence (default 0.9)
 - freshness_seconds <= reachability_max_staleness (default 30s)

3) burn_rate_exceeded(region, metric, window, threshold) -> bool
- Works for errors_5xx_burn and tail_latency_burn.
- Window must be one of approved windows (e.g., 1m/5m/30m) to avoid configuration drift.

4) capacity_hard_gate(region) -> bool
- True if headroom below threshold AND capacity signal confidence is high.
- Intended to prevent shifting into an already overloaded region.

5) corroborated(primary_signal, secondary_signal) -> bool
- Enforces ADR-042 “required corroboration signals” when configured.
- Example: if tail latency burn triggers, require either 5xx burn OR reachability degraded/down OR control plane degraded.

6) hold_down_active(last_flip_at, min_hold_down_seconds) -> bool
- If true, policy engine returns HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative.

7) flip_budget_ok(tenant_id, route_id, max_flips_per_hour) -> bool
- Input includes a precomputed counter from controller/state store (policy engine does not store state).

8) blast_radius_ok(tenant_tier, requested_action) -> bool
- Enforces “can’t shift more than X% traffic for tier Y without approval”.
- For Hosted, blast radius is route-scoped; for Dedicated, pool-scoped.

B) Deterministic evaluation mode (required)
- Add an “evaluation_mode” field:
 - recommend: compute decision + evidence; do not mark as executable
 - enforce: compute decision; include explicit requested_action(s)
- Engine must produce identical decision_type and evidence in both modes (action packaging differs).

C) Signal hierarchy evaluation (ADR-042)
Priority order (proposed canonical order for v1):
1) Reachability DOWN (authoritative) => FAILOVER (unless no healthy fallback)
2) Errors (5xx) fast burn (high severity) => FAILOVER or PARTIAL_SHIFT depending on blast radius and capacity
3) Tail latency burn (p99/p95) => PARTIAL_SHIFT first; escalate to FAILOVER if corroborated and sustained
4) Capacity exhaustion / hard gate => HOLD + load shed (controller action), avoid shifting into constrained region
5) Control plane degradation => HOLD (do not flip rapidly; prevent oscillation)

Notes:
- “No healthy fallback” means every eligible fallback region fails capacity_hard_gate OR reachability is down OR stale beyond threshold.
- If no healthy fallback, decision should be HOLD and include “degrade_allowed=true” hint (controller can activate load shedding / retry-after).

D) Policy language / config schema additions
Add new fields (names tentative):
- failover:
 - enabled: boolean
 - eligible_regions: [us-east, eu-west, ...]
 - signal_requirements:
 - primary_trigger: enum
 - corroboration: [enum]
 - min_confidence: float
 - max_staleness_seconds: int
 - dampening:
 - min_hold_down_seconds: int
 - require_sustain_seconds: int (for non-reachability triggers)
 - safety:
 - require_approval: boolean (default true for prod initially)
 - max_flips_per_hour: int
 - max_traffic_shift_percent: int
 - rollback:
 - auto_rollback_enabled: boolean
 - rollback_after_seconds: int
 - rollback_require_healthy_primary_seconds: int

E) Output schema
Decision output (single object, JSON):
- decision_id (stable hash of route_id + tenant_id + evaluation_time + policy_version)
- policy_version
- evaluation_time
- decision_type
- chosen_reason
- target_state (string encoding; owned by controller)
- requested_actions (string encoding; empty in recommend mode)
- evidence (string encoding; ordered)
- annotations (string encoding; includes thresholds, staleness, hold-down state)

Note: In our implementation we’ll likely use structured objects, but for logging/audit we must generate a stable, versioned string representation.

Safety constraints (ADR-043 alignment)
- Anti-flap:
 - Enforce hold-down between flips for non-reachability triggers.
 - Any rollback decision must respect a separate rollback hold-down (avoid ping-pong between primary and fallback).
- Rate limiting:
 - flip_budget_ok must be true, else HOLD.
- Approval hooks:
 - If require_approval is true, decision_type can still be FAILOVER but requested_actions must be empty and “approval_required=true” annotation set.
- Tenant/tier gates:
 - Enterprise/Dedicated can be configured with stricter “do not cross data residency boundary” constraint (policy engine should surface “constraint_violation:data_residency” rather than attempt partial shifts).

Edge cases and expected behavior
1) Partial outage in primary region
- Reachability degraded (not down), 5xx burn elevated, capacity OK in fallback.
- Expected: PARTIAL_SHIFT (e.g., shift 25–50% depending on max_traffic_shift_percent) if corroborated. If sustained and escalates to reachability down or error burn becomes severe => FAILOVER.

2) Signal missing / ingestion delayed
- Any authoritative signal is stale beyond max_staleness_seconds.
- Expected: HOLD. Evidence must explicitly call out staleness and which signal blocked action.

3) Fallback region constrained
- Primary is failing (5xx burn), fallback capacity_hard_gate true.
- Expected: HOLD + annotate “fallback_unhealthy_due_to_capacity”. Controller should invoke load shedding and retry-after rather than shifting load.

4) Control plane degraded
- Control plane health degraded; data plane signals ambiguous.
- Expected: HOLD unless reachability down is authoritative. (Avoid flipping policies when control plane is suspect.)

5) Multi-fallback selection
- If multiple eligible fallback regions are healthy, selection tie-breakers:
 1) policy-specified order
 2) lowest latency probe (if available in inputs)
 3) highest capacity headroom
 4) stable sort by region name

Testing plan (draft)
Unit tests
- Determinism:
 - Same payload with randomized key order => same decision_id, decision_type, evidence ordering.
- Staleness gating:
 - Stale error burn + fresh reachability OK => HOLD.
- Priority:
 - Reachability DOWN overrides hold-down.
 - 5xx burn overrides latency burn when both exceed thresholds.

Integration tests
- Replay recorded signal snapshots from staging incidents + controlled game day traces.
- Validate output is compatible with controller dry-run UX (must contain reasons + evidence).

Performance considerations
- Evaluation must be cheap; do not add per-eval remote calls.
- Evidence strings must be bounded in size. Cap rejected_candidates and evidence list.

Operational / observability hooks
- Emit a single log line per decision with:
 - decision_id, route_id, tenant_id (hashed in shared Hosted contexts), decision_type, chosen_reason
 - key thresholds and freshness
- Export metrics:
 - policy_engine_decisions_total{decision_type, chosen_reason, tier}
 - policy_engine_hold_reasons_total{reason}
 - policy_engine_eval_latency_ms

Open questions
- Exact shape of “target_state” string: should it be a controller-owned serialization of desired weights, or should the policy engine output high-level intent only?
- Do we want PARTIAL_SHIFT as a first-class decision type (recommended), or represent it as FAILOVER with weight < 100%?
- How strict should corroboration be for tail latency burn? (ADR-042 indicates corroboration required; we need the exact default set.)
- Where should data residency constraints live?
 - Option A: policy engine validates “region set allowed” and blocks action.
 - Option B: upstream policy compilation prevents invalid eligible_regions.

Near-term next steps
- Align with Miles/Ravi on canonical signal enum + reason enum.
- Draft schema PR for policy config additions (behind feature flag).
- Implement deterministic ordering + evidence output in policy engine.
- Wire to dry-run mode (ENG-2415) so the controller can display “recommended action + confidence + evidence” on game day.

Appendix: candidate enums (WIP)
chosen_reason
- REACHABILITY_DOWN
- ERROR_BURN_FAST
- LATENCY_BURN_SUSTAINED
- CAPACITY_HARD_GATE
- SIGNALS_STALE
- HOLD_DOWN_ACTIVE
- FLIP_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
- CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION_DATA_RESIDENCY
- NO_HEALTHY_FALLBACK

signal_type
- REACHABILITY
- ERRORS_5XX_BURN
- TAIL_LATENCY_BURN
- CAPACITY_HEADROOM
- CONTROL_PLANE_HEALTH

title: PRD: Quantization & Fidelity Experimentation Lab
author: Ivy Chen
text:
Summary:
This PRD defines the Quantization & Fidelity Experimentation Lab (the Lab): a reproducible, service-backed environment for running targeted fidelity experiments when introducing quantized model variants, pruning, or other cost-saving serving techniques. The Lab's outputs are deterministic experiment artifacts, decision signals (pass/fail/gated), and standardized reports used by Product, Applied ML, and Serving Runtime to decide rollouts and fallback strategies.

Goals:
- Provide a single source of truth for fidelity impact of any automated compression or quantization profile across representative tenant workloads.
- Produce machine-readable experiment results (quality deltas, latency/cost deltas, statistical significance) and a human-readable report with recommended rollout gating (allow, canary, block).
- Support experiment types: full-model quantization, per-layer mixed-precision, activation pruning, low-rank adapters, and forced KV-cache eviction behaviors.
- Integrate with the Optimize and Serving Runtime rollout pipelines to automatically recommend safe rollouts and guardrail thresholds.

Non-goals:
- The Lab will not itself perform live production A/B rollouts. It produces evidence and artifacts consumed by the rollout systems.
- The Lab does not replace long-term model quality monitoring (that remains in Console/Optimize).

Success metrics (first 6 months):
- 90% of candidate quantization profiles produce a deterministic Lab report within 48 hours of submission (on standard profiles).
- >=75% reduction in manual evaluation time for quantization-related rollouts (measured via engineering survey).
- Fallbacks triggered by Lab-approved rollback policies reduce customer-seen quality regressions by >60% vs ad-hoc rollouts.

Stakeholders and owners:
- Product (owner): Ivy Chen (product lead) — defines acceptance criteria and experimental matrix templates.
- Applied ML (owner): Rafael Ortega — curates evaluation sets and quality metrics per workload/domain.
- Eng: Serving Runtime (owner): Arjun Malhotra — provides runtime hooks and cost/latency telemetry, implements automated rollout integration.
- Eng: DevEx — SDK/CLI for experiment submission and artifacts retrieval.

User stories:
1) As an Applied ML engineer, I want to submit a quantization profile and a list of evaluation prompt sets and receive a standardized fidelity report (metrics, significance, artifact links) so I can recommend rollout policy.
2) As a Product manager, I want a summary dashboard showing pass/fail across customer segments, so I can prioritize safe rollouts.
3) As an SRE, I want experiment artifacts to include traceable request IDs and telemetry so I can audit regressions that reach production.

Experiment runner requirements (functional):
- Accept experiment definitions as YAML or JSON via SDK/REST and return a job id.
- Run experiments against: canonical test harness (deterministic RNG seeds), a configurable subset of model variants (float32, int8, 4-bit mixed), and a set of workload slices (chat, code, long-form completion, embeddings).
- Capture and persist: per-example outputs, token-level latencies, resource utilization (GPU RAM, kernels used), and per-example quality scores.
- Produce a structured report containing: aggregated metrics (mean, median, p99), delta vs baseline, 95% confidence intervals, A/B test p-values, and an automated pass/fail recommendation based on policy.

Experiment runner requirements (non-functional):
- Turnaround: typical small experiments complete within 24 - 48 hours; pilot-level experiments (large prompt sets) within 5 days.
- Reproducibility: experiments run with immutable seeds, pinned model binaries, and environment hashes.
- Multi-tenant safety: experiments run in an isolated namespace, with no customer data used unless explicitly authorized and scrubbed.

Quality metrics and gating logic:
- Primary metrics per workload:
 - Chat/Completion: semantic similarity (embedding cosine) vs baseline, normalized F1 when applicable, and response length parity. Gate: mean embedding cosine drop <= 0.012 AND 99th-percentile semantic delta <= 0.02.
 - Code generation: pass@k and compilation success rate. Gate: pass@1 drop <= 1.5 percentage points and compile-failure delta <= 0.5pp.
 - Embeddings: mean cosine similarity drop <= 0.015; downstream retrieval MAP drop <= 0.8%.
 - Latency/Cost: p50 latency must not increase more than 8% for the target serving configuration; cost/unit must be reduced by >= 12% to be considered.
- Automated pass/fail decision algorithm:
 1. Compute per-workload deltas and CIs.
 2. If any primary metric breaches gate thresholds -> FAIL.
 3. If primary metrics pass but secondary metrics (edge-case slices) show regressions above 95th-percentile thresholds -> WARN (manual review).
 4. Produce recommendation: allow | canary (10% traffic) | block.

Experiment definition schema (example YAML):
 ---
 experiment_name: "int4-mixed-prune-v2"
 model_variant: "redwood-open-7b-v2"
 baseline_variant: "redwood-open-7b-fp16"
 profiles:
 - name: "int4-mixed"
 quantization: "mixed-int4"
 per_layer_overrides: ["attn-16:8", "mlp-5:4"]
 workload_slices:
 - name: "customer-chat-small"
 sample_set: "canonical/chat-1000"
 metrics: ["embed_cosine","mean_length","toxicity_rate"]
 eval_repeat: 3
 rng_seed: 41321

Telemetry and artifact requirements:
- Events captured: experiment.submitted, experiment.started, example.{id}.inference.start, example.{id}.inference.end, experiment.completed, experiment.report.generated.
- Telemetry must include: job_id, model_variant, profile_hash, seed, environment_hash, worker_version, and timestamps.
- Artifacts stored: raw outputs (per example), normalized metric table (CSV), aggregated report (JSON and human-readable markdown), and an immutable experiment metadata file.

Data handling and PII policy:
- No customer PII may be used in Lab experiments unless explicitly consented and processed in a restricted workspace.
- When customer data is approved, the Lab will apply automated scrubbing per the Data Management policy: remove names, tokens matching credit-card patterns, and PII heuristics.

Integration points and automation:
- Rollout Integration: Lab will call the Rollout Recommendation API with pass/canary/block and attach experiment artifact links. Serving Runtime will annotate model variants with experiment ids.
- Console: Add a new page type "Experiment Report" where product and applied-ml can browse experiments, filter by model, and export PDFs.
- CLI: redwood-lab submit --file experiment.yaml -> returns job id; redwood-lab report --id JOB -> downloads artifacts.

Operational requirements and infra sizing:
- Baseline test cluster: 8x A100(80GB) equivalent nodes for parallel small experiments; ability to burst to 32 nodes for large sweeps.
- Storage: lifecycle retention of experiment artifacts: 90 days hot, 1 year cold archive.
- RBAC: roles: lab-admin, lab-runner, lab-viewer. lab-runner may execute jobs but cannot delete artifacts.

Reporting and human-readable output (example):
Title: int4-mixed-prune-v2 — redwood-open-7b-v2
Summary: Pass with WARN on edge-case legal prompts. p50 latency -3.4%, cost/unit -18.7%
Primary metrics table:
| workload | baseline | variant | delta | CI95 | decision |
| chat-1000 | 0.872 | 0.861 | -0.011 | ±0.003 | PASS |
| legal-slice | 0.790 | 0.760 | -0.030 | ±0.010 | WARN |
Notes: The legal-slice regression is concentrated in documents with very long citations (see artifact: /artifacts/12345/legal-edge-cases.csv). Recommend a canary to 5% with automated fallback to fp16 for flagged tenant tags.

Rollout gating workflow (recommended):
1. Experiment authorates PRD + attaches Lab report.
2. Applied ML reviews WARNs; if minor, mark canary; if block, require engineer to iterate.
3. If canary approved, schedule a 2-week canary at 5-10% traffic with monitoring alerts configured (quality delta, token-level fraud checks).
4. If canary succeeds (no production quality regression for 14 days), promote to gradual rollout.

Testing, QA, and guardrails:
- Unit tests: experiment runner validation logic, schema conformance.
- Integration tests: end-to-end run against a small synthetic workload with deterministic outputs.
- Chaos test: randomly kill runner nodes; verify retry semantics and artifact integrity.
- Guardrails: experiments that touch PII require approval from Data Governance.

Open questions and risks:
- How to budget the infra cost of large sweep experiments vs. business value? (Mitigation: quota-based submission and cost-credits workflow.)
- Potential overfitting to canonical prompt sets. (Mitigation: require at least one customer representative slice for any production rollout.)

Milestones and roadmap (quarterly):
- Q1: MVP experiment runner, CLI, and basic report generation; integrate with Rollout Recommendation API.
- Q2: Support for mixed-precision per-layer overrides, artifact retention policy, and Console report UI.
- Q3: Auto-recommendations tied to Optimize insights (cost/latency tradeoff visualizer) and canary orchestration link.

Appendix: example CLI usage and minimal SDK snippet
# Submit
redwood-lab submit --file int4-experiment.yaml
# Poll
redwood-lab status --id job-20270322-001
# Fetch report
redwood-lab report --id job-20270322-001 --output ./reports/job-001

Python SDK (pseudo):
from redwood.lab import LabClient
client = LabClient()
job = client.submit(experiment_definition)
report = client.wait_and_fetch(job.id)
print(report.summary)

Ownership and contacts:
- Product lead: Ivy Chen (ivy@redwood.com)
- Applied ML lead: Rafael Ortega (rafael@redwood.com)
- Serving Runtime lead: Arjun Malhotra (arjun@redwood.com)

References:
- Quality-aware quantization rollout PRD (internal) — /confluence/product-docs/requirements/quality-aware-quantization-rollout-prd-2026-12-01
- Elastic SLO cost simulator playbook — /confluence/product-docs/design-specs/elastic-slo-cost-simulator-playbook-2026-12-04
- Benchmarking & perf suite — /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite

title: Throughput-Latency Phase Portrait — mini benchmark heuristic
author: Claire Nguyen
text:
Purpose:
This is a compact, portable benchmark note that experiments with a 'phase portrait' view of throughput vs latency across three representative interactive workloads. The goal is a lightweight heuristic we can run in-console to quickly show tradeoffs between lower unit-cost throughput and percentile latencies for different model/hardware/batching choices.

Quick takeaways (TL;DR):
- For conversational short-turn workloads (turns <= 40 tokens) the H100 + small-batch multiplexing gives best p50 and p90 at moderate cost; p99 is highly sensitive to background session churn.
- For longer-turn generation (avg 300 tokens), batching (window 25–50ms) on A100-like instances recovers ~20–35% dollars-per-token vs aggressive single-request fastpath.
- Int8-quantized 34B reduces cost 40–50% at a modest p90 increase (~5–15ms) in our configs — good candidate for mid-tier SLAs.

Testbed & assumptions:
- Date: May 2029, quick lab runs in eu-west-1 dedicated test pool (sandbox).
- Models: rw-7b-fp16, rw-34b-int8, rw-70b-fp16 (representative family: small, mid, large).
- Hardware: H100x1 (80GB), A100x1 (40GB), A10Gx1 (24GB) — note: these are single-GPU node profiles run under the same runtime image.
- Network: intra-region, measured client RTT mean 5ms.
- Workloads: three profiles (interactive-nano, interactive-short, long-generate):
 * interactive-nano — 1–8 tokens output per turn, arrival Poisson lambda tuned for 400rps sustained, 10% bursts.
 * interactive-short — median 35 tokens output, targeted for chat UIs with quick replies.
 * long-generate — median 300 tokens, used by summarization/batch-response flows.
- Economic: rough spot-equivalent cost used for dollars-per-1M-tokens (includes amortized GPU runtime + networking overhead); absolute numbers are lab approximations for comparison only.

Measurement method:
- Each workload run for 15 minutes after a 2-minute warmup.
- Metrics collected: throughput (tokens/sec), p50/p90/p99 request latency (ms) measured end-to-end, throughput-utilization (GPU cycles estimated), and estimated $/1M tokens (runtime-only).
- Two modes tested per workload: fastpath (no batching, low-latency multiplexer), and windowed-batching (batch-window 25ms, max-batch 32).

Representative results (aggregated):
Note: numbers are simplified to highlight shape, not a rigorous stat-run.

1) interactive-nano (short token replies)
- rw-7b-fp16 on H100 (fastpath): throughput 9.8k tokens/s, p50 6ms, p90 14ms, p99 42ms, $/1M tok = $4.2
- rw-7b-fp16 on H100 (window25ms): throughput 16.1k tokens/s, p50 9ms, p90 22ms, p99 75ms, $/1M tok = $2.6
- rw-34b-int8 on H100 (fastpath): throughput 6.1k tokens/s, p50 12ms, p90 28ms, p99 90ms, $/1M tok = $6.8
- rw-34b-int8 on H100 (window25ms): throughput 10.9k tokens/s, p50 18ms, p90 38ms, p99 110ms, $/1M tok = $4.1

2) interactive-short (chat-like ~35 tokens)
- rw-34b-int8 on A100 (fastpath): throughput 1.1k tokens/s, p50 22ms, p90 58ms, p99 160ms, $/1M tok = $12.4
- rw-34b-int8 on A100 (window25ms): throughput 1.7k tokens/s, p50 30ms, p90 85ms, p99 210ms, $/1M tok = $8.6
- rw-70b-fp16 on H100 (fastpath): throughput 0.7k tokens/s, p50 45ms, p90 120ms, p99 380ms, $/1M tok = $28.9

3) long-generate (avg 300 tokens)
- rw-70b-fp16 on A100 (fastpath): throughput 430 tok/s, p50 310ms, p90 820ms, p99 2.7s, $/1M tok = $31.6
- rw-70b-fp16 on A100 (window50ms): throughput 560 tok/s, p50 380ms, p90 910ms, p99 3.1s, $/1M tok = $23.8
- rw-34b-int8 on A100 (window50ms): throughput 810 tok/s, p50 240ms, p90 560ms, p99 1.9s, $/1M tok = $12.7

Phase portrait sketches (ASCII) — throughput on X axis (tokens/sec), latency percentiles on Y. Each row is a rough slice per workload/config.

interactive-nano (throughput vs p90):
[ 5k ] * rw-7b fastpath p90=14ms * rw-34b fastpath p90=28ms
[10k ] * rw-7b window25 p90=22ms * rw-34b window25 p90=38ms
[15k ] * rw-7b window25 (peak)

interactive-short (throughput vs p90):
[ 0.5k ] * rw-70b fastpath p90=120ms
[ 1.0k ] * rw-34b fastpath p90=58ms
[ 1.7k ] * rw-34b window25 p90=85ms

long-generate (throughput vs p90):
[ 0.4k ] * rw-70b fastpath p90=820ms
[ 0.56k] * rw-70b window50 p90=910ms
[ 0.81k] * rw-34b window50 p90=560ms

Interpretation & guidance:
- The phase portrait exposes two useful decision axes: (1) target throughput band (tokens/sec) and (2) target percentile latency. For super-low-latency UIs (p90 < 30ms), small models on H100 with fastpath are best despite higher $/M tokens at scale.
- For mid-latency SLAs (p90 30–120ms) and cost sensitivity, rw-34b-int8 with windowed batching on A100 becomes attractive — good balance of dollars and p90.
- For heavy long generation, batching recovers material $/token improvements; pick larger batch windows (40–60ms) but watch p99 tail growth.
- p99 remains dominated by session-level jitter (session churn, cache warmups). Improving p99 will likely require admission controls or prioritized fastpaths rather than only kernel-level tuning.

Recommended knobs to surface in Console for quick decisions:
- Phase portrait toggles: select workload archetype + target percentile slider (p50/p90/p99) -> show cost delta and suggested model/hardware/batch-length.
- Quick-sim: run a 2-minute micro-run that returns an annotated portrait with estimated $/1M tok. (Use sandbox cap and fail-safe).
- Presets: low-latency (p90<30ms), balanced (p90 30–120ms), deep-generation (p90>200ms). Each preset maps to a recommended profile (model + hardware + batching).

Next steps / follow-ups:
- Run a controlled 5x repeat for a narrower confidence interval on p99 for the interactive-short profile; measure with enforced synthetic user churn.
- Add memory-pressure tests for A10G vs A100 for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Prototype the Console quick-sim and validate UX with a couple of internal customers (SEs).

Open questions / caveats:
- These runs are single-node. Multi-GPU sharding and memory-pinned tiling will change throughput curves for rw-70b; expect non-linear scaling.
- Cost numbers are lab approximations; company pricing model (Dedicated vs Hosted) will change break-evens.
- Edge region network delta (client RTT > 30ms) will shift the sweet spot toward batching for interactive workloads.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intended as a heuristic artifact for product/console decisions rather than a formal paper. Please flag any obvious omissions or ask for additional per-node profiler traces (we captured GPU utilization and nvlink counters in the raw logs).
- If this heuristic looks useful, I can port it to a small Notebook that runs inside the Console sandbox and emits the phase portrait + recommended knobs automatically.

-- Claire

title: Offline bundle format and manifest (Redwood Private on-prem/air-gapped)
author: Jordan Lee
text:
## Overview
This page defines the **offline bundle** file format used to install or upgrade **Redwood Private** in **air-gapped / offline** environments. It specifies:
- Bundle layout (directory structure + required artifacts)
- The **bundle manifest** (schema + hashing requirements)
- SBOM inclusion/pointers
- Compatibility rules (forward/backward)
- Size and packaging constraints for common offline transport workflows

This page is the source of truth for what the installer expects on disk. Signing and verification behavior is defined in the design doc and ADR (linked above).

---

## Goals
1. Enable offline install/upgrade with **no network fetches** (installer must operate fully from the bundle).
2. Provide a deterministic, machine-verifiable inventory of contents (hashes + versions).
3. Support cryptographic signing of the manifest (integrity + provenance).
4. Support incremental evolution of the bundle format without breaking older installers.

## Non-goals (initial phase)
- Customer-provided signing roots / customer-signed bundles (tracked as a future plan).
- Fully standardizing on one container transport format for all customers; we support a small set with clear rules.

---

## Terminology
- **Bundle**: The offline artifact delivered to customers (a directory or an archive that expands to a directory).
- **Bundle root**: Top-level directory containing manifest and artifact subdirectories.
- **Manifest**: Canonical file inventory and metadata; is the unit that is signed.
- **Build ID**: Unique identifier for the release build producing the bundle.

---

## Bundle root requirements
The bundle MUST expand to a single directory (the bundle root) containing the following top-level files:
- `manifest.json` (required)
- `manifest.sig` (required for signed bundles; optional only for explicitly approved break-glass bundles)
- `README.txt` (required; short human instructions, version, and support pointers)

Optional:
- `manifest.certchain.pem` (optional; included when verification expects an embedded certificate chain)
- `SBOM/` directory (optional; when SBOM is embedded rather than referenced)

The installer MUST be pointed at the bundle root directory (not at an archive). Customers may transport bundles as an archive (e.g., `.tar.zst`) but MUST extract prior to install.

---

## Directory structure (bundle layout)
### Required directories
A valid bundle contains the following directories under the bundle root:

1) `install/`
- Contains installer entrypoints and helper binaries/scripts used by Redwood Private installation and preflight.

2) `charts/`
- Helm chart tarballs (`.tgz`) required for Redwood Private components.

3) `images/`
- Offline container images in one of the supported forms (see “Container images” section).

4) `artifacts/`
- Redwood runtime artifacts required for on-prem serving (e.g., engine plugins, tokenizer assets, compatibility shims).

5) `config/`
- Offline install configuration defaults, schema files, and example values.

### Optional directories
- `models/` (optional in initial phase; when present, includes model weights or model bundles for customers approved for offline model transport)
- `deps/` (optional; OS/package dependencies only when explicitly required for a specific on-prem installer path)
- `SBOM/` (optional; embedded SBOM documents)

### Example tree
The following is an illustrative example. Exact filenames vary by release.

Bundle root:
- `manifest.json`
- `manifest.sig`
- `README.txt`
- `install/`
 - `redwood-private-installer-linux-amd64`
 - `redwood-private-installer-linux-amd64.sha256` (optional convenience checksum; not a substitute for manifest hashes)
 - `plugins/` (optional)
- `charts/`
 - `redwood-private-1.32.0.tgz`
 - `redwood-observability-1.32.0.tgz`
 - `redwood-gateway-1.32.0.tgz`
- `images/`
 - `oci-layout/` (preferred)
 - `index.json`
 - `blobs/sha256/...`
 - `images.lock` (required; references image digests; also included in manifest)
- `artifacts/`
 - `runtime/`
 - `engine-plugins-2026.01.0.tar.zst`
 - `tokenizers-2026.01.0.tar.zst`
 - `compat/`
 - `k8s-migrations-2026.01.0.tgz`
- `config/`
 - `values.schema.json`
 - `values.offline.example.yaml`
- `SBOM/` (optional)
 - `sbom.spdx.json`
 - `sbom.cyclonedx.json`

---

## Supported artifact types and rules
### Installer artifacts (`install/`)
Required:
- Exactly one platform installer binary is REQUIRED for supported platforms (initial support: Linux amd64; Linux arm64 optional by release).
- Any required helper binaries MUST be included locally; the installer must not download dependencies in air-gapped mode.

Rules:
- Filenames are included in manifest and MUST match exactly (case-sensitive).
- Executable bit must be preserved by the customer’s transfer/extract tooling. README.txt includes extraction guidance.

### Helm charts (`charts/`)
Required:
- Helm chart tarballs (`.tgz`) for all components referenced by the release.

Rules:
- Chart versions and `appVersion` MUST align with the bundle `release.version` metadata in `manifest.json`.
- The installer reads charts from this directory only; it must not attempt to pull charts from remote repos.

### Container images (`images/`)
Required:
- An offline image store plus a lock file.

Supported formats (one of):
1) **OCI image layout** (preferred)
 - Stored under `images/oci-layout/`
 - The manifest MUST include the top-level `index.json` hash plus blob hashes.
2) **Docker image tar archives** (supported only for customers with existing docker load workflows)
 - Stored as `.tar` under `images/docker-archives/`
 - The manifest MUST include sha256 hashes for the tar files and the expected image digests.

Lock file:
- `images/images.lock` is REQUIRED.
- It contains the authoritative list of image references and immutable digests (e.g., `registry.redwoodinference.com/redwood/gateway@sha256:...`).
- The lock file itself is hashed and listed in `manifest.json`.

Rules:
- Tags are allowed in lock entries for readability but digests MUST be present and treated as authoritative.
- The bundle MUST include all images referenced by charts/values for the default offline install path.

### Runtime artifacts (`artifacts/`)
Required:
- Runtime-dependent assets needed for the release (engine plugins, tokenizer assets, migration packages, etc.).

Rules:
- Artifacts must be referenced by exact filename and sha256.
- Where possible, artifacts should be compressed using `.tar.zst` for size efficiency.

### Config assets (`config/`)
Required:
- Offline example values files and schemas used for validation.

Rules:
- These files are treated as install inputs and MUST be hashed.

### SBOM (`SBOM/` or external reference)
SBOM is REQUIRED at the release level, provided either:
- Embedded in the bundle at `SBOM/` and referenced from the manifest with hashes, OR
- Referenced externally via a pointer in the manifest (pointer MUST include content hash), for customers who prefer separate SBOM distribution channels.

---

## Manifest: required files and signing
### Files
- `manifest.json` (required)
- `manifest.sig` (required for normal releases)

The signature covers the canonical bytes of `manifest.json` (canonicalization rules are owned by ADR-0147; this page specifies the semantic schema).

---

## Manifest schema (semantic specification)
`manifest.json` MUST be a UTF-8 JSON document.

### Required top-level fields
- `schema_version`: Version of the manifest schema (e.g., `"1.0"`).
- `bundle`: Bundle identity fields (id, format version).
- `release`: Redwood Private release metadata (version, channel).
- `build`: Build provenance metadata (build id, timestamps, repo SHAs).
- `artifacts`: List of all files/artifacts covered by the manifest, including their hashes.
- `sbom`: SBOM pointer(s) and hashes.

### Recommended/optional top-level fields
- `compatibility`: Installer version constraints and upgrade/downgrade rules.
- `notes`: Human-readable summary (kept short; do not include secrets).

### Required per-artifact fields
Each artifact entry MUST include:
- `path`: Relative path from bundle root using `/` separators.
- `sha256`: Lowercase hex sha256 digest of the file content.
- `size_bytes`: File size in bytes.
- `type`: One of: `installer`, `helm_chart`, `image_lock`, `image_store`, `runtime_artifact`, `config`, `sbom`, `model`, `dep`, `other`.

Optional per-artifact fields (when applicable):
- `media_type`: Helpful descriptor (e.g., `application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`, `application/gzip`).
- `image_digests`: For image stores/archives, a comma-separated list of image digests expected to be present.
- `chart`: For charts, `name` and `version` as a single string `"<name>@<version>"`.

### SBOM section
The manifest MUST include at least one SBOM reference:
- `sbom.primary_path` (relative path) OR `sbom.primary_uri` (external location)
- `sbom.primary_sha256`

Optional:
- `sbom.formats` as a comma-separated list (e.g., `spdx-json,cyclonedx-json`)
- `sbom.secondary_paths` as a comma-separated list of additional embedded SBOMs

### Compatibility section
If present, `compatibility` MUST include:
- `min_installer_version`: Minimum installer version required to verify/install this bundle.
- `max_tested_installer_version`: Highest installer version validated during CI for this release (informational).
- `downgrade_policy`: `forbid` or `allow_with_flag` (default: `forbid`).

---

## Manifest example (illustrative)
(For readability, formatted here; actual file must follow canonicalization rules for signing as defined in ADR-0147.)

{
 "schema_version": "1.0",
 "bundle": {
 "format": "redwood-private-offline-bundle",
 "format_version": "1",
 "bundle_id": "rbwpriv-2026.01.0+build.18492",
 "created_at": "2026-01-12T03:41:22Z"
 },
 "release": {
 "product": "redwood-private",
 "version": "2026.01.0",
 "channel": "stable"
 },
 "build": {
 "build_id": "build.18492",
 "pipeline": "private-release",
 "git": "redwood-private-installer@9f3c2a1,redwood-helm-charts@4b1d0c9,redwood@c2de88a"
 },
 "compatibility": {
 "min_installer_version": "1.18.0",
 "max_tested_installer_version": "1.19.2",
 "downgrade_policy": "forbid"
 },
 "sbom": {
 "primary_path": "SBOM/sbom.spdx.json",
 "primary_sha256": "<sha256>",
 "formats": "spdx-json,cyclonedx-json",
 "secondary_paths": "SBOM/sbom.cyclonedx.json"
 },
 "artifacts": [
 {
 "path": "install/redwood-private-installer-linux-amd64",
 "sha256": "<sha256>",
 "size_bytes": "48219312",
 "type": "installer"
 },
 {
 "path": "charts/redwood-private-1.32.0.tgz",
 "sha256": "<sha256>",
 "size_bytes": "913422",
 "type": "helm_chart",
 "chart": "redwood-private@1.32.0"
 },
 {
 "path": "images/images.lock",
 "sha256": "<sha256>",
 "size_bytes": "18492",
 "type": "image_lock"
 },
 {
 "path": "images/oci-layout/index.json",
 "sha256": "<sha256>",
 "size_bytes": "7312",
 "type": "image_store",
 "media_type": "application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json"
 },
 {
 "path": "artifacts/runtime/engine-plugins-2026.01.0.tar.zst",
 "sha256": "<sha256>",
 "size_bytes": "182390112",
 "type": "runtime_artifact"
 }
 ],
 "notes": "Signed offline bundle for Redwood Private 2026.01.0 (stable)."
}

---

## Hashing requirements
- `sha256` is the required hash algorithm for all artifacts.
- Hashes MUST be computed on the exact bytes of the file as stored in the bundle.
- For archives (e.g., `.tgz`, `.tar.zst`, `.tar`), hash the archive file itself (not expanded contents).

Common transfer pitfalls to call out in support:
- Repackaging archives can change bytes and invalidate hashes.
- “Smart unzip” or antivirus tools can modify files or strip executable bits.

---

## Backward/forward compatibility policy
### General rule
- Installers MUST fail closed if required fields are missing or any required artifact hash mismatches.
- Installers MUST ignore unknown fields (forward-compatible) unless the field is explicitly declared “critical” by installer version.

### Manifest schema versioning
- `schema_version` uses `MAJOR.MINOR` semantics.
 - MINOR increments may add optional fields or new artifact types.
 - MAJOR increments may introduce breaking changes; will require a new minimum installer version.

### Bundle format versioning
- `bundle.format_version` is an integer representing the on-disk layout expectations.
- The installer MUST check `bundle.format` and `bundle.format_version` and error if unsupported.

### Artifact type extensibility
- New `type` values may be added. Installers should treat unknown `type` values as `other` for display/inspection, but still enforce hash verification for those files if they are referenced in `artifacts`.

---

## Size and packaging constraints
### Practical constraints (customer environments)
Air-gapped customers frequently move bundles via:
- Secure file transfer to a staging host inside the enclave
- Removable media with filesystem limits (notably FAT32 4 GiB file limit)
- Offline scanning/ingestion systems with maximum object size policies

### Redwood guidance
- Target bundle size (typical release, excluding optional models): **≤ 60 GiB**.
- Hard limit for standard supportability: **≤ 120 GiB**.
- If a release would exceed 120 GiB, Release Engineering must:
 - Provide a documented split-bundle strategy OR
 - Obtain explicit Product + Security approval with customer-specific guidance.

### Split bundle policy (when needed)
If split delivery is used, the following rules apply:
- Each part must be independently hashable and referenced from the manifest.
- The installer must support a deterministic reassembly method (documented in README.txt).
- Split bundle mechanics MUST NOT change the bytes of `manifest.json` post-signing.

Note: Current default path is single bundle directory; split delivery is supported only for approved customers and must be coordinated with Solutions/PS.

---

## README.txt requirements (customer-facing summary)
`README.txt` MUST include:
- Product + release version
- Bundle ID + build ID
- Minimum installer version
- Simple extraction guidance (including preserving executable bits)
- Primary verification command (e.g., `installer inspect --verify`)
- Log locations for verification failures
- Support escalation pointers

Do not include secrets, internal URLs that won’t resolve in air-gapped environments, or customer-specific tokens.

---

## Validation checklist (what CI and local tooling must enforce)
A bundle is considered well-formed if:
1. Required top-level files exist: `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `README.txt`.
2. All `artifacts[].path` entries exist on disk and are within the bundle root (no `..` traversal).
3. All artifact hashes and sizes match.
4. `schema_version`, `bundle.format`, and `bundle.format_version` are supported.
5. `images/images.lock` exists and is included in `artifacts`.
6. SBOM is present (embedded or pointer) and hash is verifiable.
7. No network fetch is required for default offline install path.

---

## Open items / future extensions
- Standardizing model transport under `models/` (including chunking and license attestation).
- Optional inclusion of per-artifact `sha512` for customers requiring dual-hash policies.
- Formal definition of “critical unknown fields” (installer behavior) tied to schema version.

---

## Ownership
- Format/layout + installer expectations: **Eng Private Deployments** (Ethan Park)
- Manifest schema + canonicalization: **Deterministic policy/manifest engineering** (Jordan Lee) in collaboration with Release Eng
- Signing and key management: **Release Engineering / Security Engineering** (Connor O'Brien, Marcus Lin)
- Docs and customer guidance: **DevEx** (Kira Thompson)

title: Developer Onramp: Localization, Docs-site Ops, and Canonical Fixes Playbook
author: Marisol Vega
text:
Overview

This playbook bundles three tightly related areas that frequently cause onboarding friction for new integrations: SDK localization (i18n) readiness, docs-site operational procedures (staging/canary/translation pipelines), and a compact set of canonical fixes for the top support issues we see from developer onramps. The goal is a one-page operational reference that engineering, Docs, and Support can use during new SDK ship weeks and customer trials.

Goals
- Reduce mean-time-to-first-success (MTTFS) for new SDK adopters by 30% through localized examples and a repeatable docs deploy pipeline.
- Provide concise canonical fixes for the top 8 devx support issues so Support can resolve 60% of triageable tickets without engineering intervention.
- Maintain a low-friction docs release process (canary -> staged -> prod) with clear rollback semantics and telemetry hooks.

Audience
- Developer Experience engineers and tech writers shipping SDK examples and docs.
- Support engineers handling integration issues and reproductions.
- Product engineers owning SDKs or client libraries.

Scope and non-goals
- Included: JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Go SDK snippets; docs-site content lifecycle; translation handoff and CI checks; canonical fixes for common API/SDK errors.
- Excluded: full localization of legal or marketing copy; mobile SDKs beyond sample snippets.

Prerequisites
1) Repo layout: all SDK examples live under repo: redwood/devx-examples (branch: main).
2) Docs-site: hosted via docs.redwood-inference.internal, uses static site generator with i18n plugin (locales in /i18n/*.json).
3) CI: GitHub Actions with workflows: docs-canary.yml, docs-staged.yml, docs-prod.yml.
4) Telemetry: snippet telemetry.events.example_load, telemetry.tags.locale, and telemetry.context.sdk_version must be emitted by sample harness.

Quickstart: Localized SDK Example Bundle (developer flow)
1. Clone examples: git clone git@github.com:redwood/devx-examples.git && cd devx-examples
2. Install toolchain (node/pip/go): ./scripts/bootstrap-dev.sh
3. Generate locale-specific examples: ./scripts/generate-localized-examples --locales=en,es,fr --sdk=python
4. Run local docs server including translations: npm run docs:local -- --locale=fr
5. Verify telemetry events appear in staging stream (kinesis-devx-staging): 
 - Expected event: {"event":"example_load","locale":"fr","sdk":"python","version":"0.12.0"}
6. Submit PR to docs-examples with i18n diffs and request docs-site canary deploy via label: docs-canary-request

SDK Localization Checklist (per release)
- [ ] Confirm sample text keys are externalized (no hard-coded English strings in code examples).
- [ ] Provide translation-ready README and example captions in /i18n/{locale}.json.
- [ ] Localized code comments: keep English primary, add short localized caption lines under // LOCAL: ... to avoid syntax churn.
- [ ] Add locale-specific smoke tests: tests/smoke/{locale}/example_test.py (asserts example runs and emits telemetry).
- [ ] Bump telemetry schema version if adding fields: TELEMETRY_SCHEMA: v2 -> notify analytics@redwood.com.

Table: Supported Example Locales and Priority
Locale | Priority | Owner | Notes
------ | -------- | ----- | -----
en (English) | high | devx-eng | baseline; all CI gates run against en
es (Spanish) | medium | intl-ops | customer-facing regions: LATAM, EU-ES
fr (French) | medium | intl-ops | EU-FR customers
de (German) | low | intl-ops | add on request
ja (Japanese) | low | intl-ops | APAC pilot only

Docs-site Operating Procedure (canary -> staged -> prod)
1) Authoring and PRs
 - Create content branch in docs-content repo and include locale JSONs under /i18n.
 - Attach smoke test run output to PR (artifact: smoke-{sha}.zip).
 - Tag PR with labels: [docs-canary-request] or [docs-staged-request] as appropriate.
2) Canary deploy (automatic with label docs-canary-request)
 - Action: GitHub Action docs-canary.yml runs build and deploys to docs-canary.redwood-inference.internal.
 - Checks (must pass): build (exit 0), i18n-linter (no missing keys), smoke-tests (artifacts present), telemetry sanity (at least one example_load event during smoke test).
 - Rollback: manual; revert PR or trigger docs-canary-rollback workflow.
3) Staged deploy (after 48h of Canary uptime and signoff)
 - Add label docs-staged-request. Ops lead runs gated promote: ./tools/promote_docs.sh --from=canary --to=staged --approve="<approver>"
 - Staged URL: docs-staged.redwood-inference.internal. Run translation QA with translator team.
4) Prod promote
 - Window: M-F 9:00-17:00 PT. Approvals: 2 reviewers (author + docs eng). Run promote script with --to=prod and monitor SLOs for 30min.

Operational SLOs for Docs-site during promote windows
- Build success rate >= 99% (30-day rolling).
- Canary smoke-tests pass within 15 minutes after deploy.
- No production downtime > 1 minute caused by new docs push.

Canonical Support Issues and Fixes (top issues during onramp)
Issue A: SDK example fails to authenticate (401)
- Detection: error pattern in logs: "error=unauthorized, code=401, hint=apiKey"; Support: run reproduction script with -v flag.
- Root cause: sample uses environment variable REDWOOD_API_KEY unset or using expired demo key.
- Canonical fix steps:
 1. Confirm env var exists: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY
 2. If missing, instruct customer to create API key via console (link: internal:product-docs/create-api-key).
 3. For expired keys, rotate and confirm permission scopes: scopes must include: [inference:invoke, metrics:read].
 4. Add small code snippet to sample that fails fast with helpful error message (example below).
- Owner: Support -> escalate to SDK owner if repro fails.

Code snippet: fail-fast auth check (Python)
```python
import os
api_key = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
if not api_key:
 raise RuntimeError('Missing REDWOOD_API_KEY environment variable. Create one at https://console.redwood-inference.internal/settings/api-keys')
# proceed with client
```

Issue B: Streaming responses stall mid-stream
- Detection: client receives first tokens then stalls; metrics show open connection but no bytes.
- Root cause: client-level keepalive mismatch or proxy buffering (common with corporate proxies).
- Canonical fix steps:
 1. Ask customer to test with curl -N to confirm raw stream: 
 curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -N \"https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/stream?...\"
 2. If curl works, recommend SDK change: prefer chunked transfer decoding and set socket keepalive: true.
 3. Provide fallback example using poll-based generation with polling timeout 5s.
- Owner: SDK eng + DevX docs for the streaming troubleshooting page.

Issue C: Localized examples missing strings or have placeholders ("__MISSING__")
- Detection: i18n-linter failure in CI; smoke test asserts replaceable keys remain.
- Root cause: upstream translations not merged to branch or translation key mismatch after refactor.
- Canonical fix steps:
 1. Run i18n-linter locally: npm run i18n-lint -- --locale=es
 2. Check missing keys report: ./tools/i18n-report --sha <pr-sha>
 3. If keys changed upstream, rebase PR and run ./scripts/merge-i18n.sh
 4. If translation missing, create placeholder and flag translator for fast-turn merge.
- Owner: Docs + Intl-ops.

Issue D: SDK telemetry not appearing in staging (no example_load events)
- Detection: telemetry dashboard shows zero events for smoke-run timeframe.
- Root cause: SDK example uses wrong telemetry endpoint, or telemetry schema mismatch.
- Canonical fix steps:
 1. Confirm telemetry endpoint env var: TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT points to staging ingestion.
 2. Run smoke tests locally with verbose flag and inspect emitted payloads: ./scripts/run-smoke --verbose | jq .
 3. If schema mismatch, check TELEMETRY_SCHEMA in repo and bump analytics contract.
- Owner: DevX instrumentation owner.

Emergency rollback recipe (docs-site)
- Trigger: Canary or staged build causes widespread example breakage or production regressions.
- Steps:
 1. Revert offending PR or tag immediately. Use GitHub UI or: git revert --no-edit <merge-commit> && push.
 2. Run docs-canary-rollback action: ./tools/docs_rollback --env=canary --commit=<last-good-commit>
 3. Notify #devx and #sre-channels with incident summary template (include commit, author, time).
 4. Run postmortem within 72 hours if > 15 developer-impacting incidents occurred.

Telemetry and Monitoring (what to watch)
- Telemetry events: example_load, example_error, docs_build_status
- Dashboards: DevX -> Examples Overview, Docs -> Build Health, Support -> Top SDK Errors
- Alerts: Build failure rate > 5% in 1h (PagerDuty to Docs oncall), Missing telemetry events for a deployed smoke run (Slack alert to #devx-monitor).

Owner matrix and contact points
- DevX Docs (authoring + i18n): Marisol Vega (owner)
- Intl-ops (translation & QA): Sana Ribeiro
- SDK engineering (runtime fixes): Evan Park
- Support triage lead: Luis Moreno

Appendix: Example file layout (minimal)
- /devx-examples/
 - /python/
 - example_quickstart.py
 - README.md
 - /i18n/en.json
 - /i18n/es.json
 - /js/
 - example_quickstart.js
 - /i18n/en.json

Contact and escalation
- For blocked promotes contact: #devx-ops on Slack and add pager: docs-oncall@redwood-inference.internal
- For telemetry contract questions: analytics@redwood-inference.internal

Revision history
- 2025-09-12: Initial draft by Marisol Vega
- 2025-11-03: Added streaming troubleshooting and telemetry checks (review: Evan Park)
- 2026-02-20: Finalized canary/staged procedure and rollback script path updates

Related artifacts and snippets
- Scripts referenced live in repo: https://github.com/redwood/devx-examples/tree/main/scripts
- Translation handoff template: /templates/translation-handoff.md

End of playbook

Subject: Executive OKRs: headcount allocation checklist & freeze exceptions

Team —

QBR prep note: the execs want a clean headcount allocation table tied to our OKRs by the end of next week. I've attached QBR_headcount_model_v2.xlsx (baseline + two scenarios). Please do the following and reply in-thread by EOD Friday (06/04):

1) For your org, list up to three hires you consider top-priority for hitting current OKRs (name the role, justification tied to specific OKR, expected start quarter).
2) Flag any backfills that are must-fill vs can-wait. Include cost delta (annual fully-loaded) if possible.
3) If you need an exception to the hiring freeze, complete the attached freeze-exception-form.pdf and include a 2–3 line business impact statement.

I'm particularly focused on: Serving/runtime (latency OKR), Platform (reliability SLO), and Sales (net-new ARR). We have a constrained budget scenario (see tab: Scenario B) — if you can provide prioritized trade-offs (e.g., freeze swap a junior SWE for a senior infra engineer), include them.

title: 1769994321-euc2-eks-spot-gpu-provisioning.json
text:
maria: Starting EKS bootstrap for eu-central-2. Goal: GPU spot nodegroup for batch inference + small ondemand infra pool for agents and monitoring.
aj: Good. Drop the preflight checklist here so I can verify quotas and SGs.
maria: Preflight checklist: 1) Request ENI & IPv4 quota increases; 2) Create VPC w/ 3 AZ subnets (/24); 3) Approve GPU instance families (p3/p4) in billing console; 4) Prepare eksctl cluster YAML + nodegroup specs; 5) Install NVIDIA operator + device plugin; 6) Tag subnets + cluster for internal ELB; 7) Run driver & infer smoke tests; 8) Handoff to oncall with logs.
devon: Reminder from ap-south incident: ENI limits are often tiny in new regs. Verify ENI-per-instance for chosen instance type: `aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types p4d.24xlarge --query 'InstanceTypes[].NetworkInfo'`. Also check elastic network interface quotas.
aj: I'll file quota ticket (AWS-987654) for ENI and EIP increases and request EFA if needed for NCCL tests.
maria: Nodegroup plan: gpu-spot (capacityType: SPOT, tainted, label role=gpu) + infra-ondemand (small t3/t4 family). Using standard eksctl AMIs for now; Bottlerocket deferred.
samir: How are we installing NVIDIA drivers? Operator or manual daemonset? Operator simplifies upgrades but had issues in v2.
devon: We prefer NVIDIA GPU Operator (current stable). Install flow: `kubectl create ns gpu-operator` then apply operator manifest from the verified tag. Verify pods come up in gpu-operator ns.
aj: Kubelet notes: ensure kubeletExtraArgs include any required feature gates for device plugins and set `--fail-swap-on=false` if using some base AMIs. For maxPods we may want to tune `maxPods` in nodegroup config for p4 nodes.
maria: For spot pool, add label `capacityType=SPOT` and taint `spot=true:PreferNoSchedule` so batch scheduler can tolerate. We'll use PodDisruptionBudgets and retry logic to handle preemptions.
devon: If job consolidation & bin-packing is critical consider Karpenter instead of ASG. Karpenter needs separate IAM role + instance profile and is more flexible for GPU scheduling.
samir: Smoke test snippet: `kubectl run gpu-check --image=nvidia/cuda:11.8-base --rm -it --restart=Never -- nvidia-smi` and then run a lightweight inference container to validate CUDA & cuDNN.
aj: Network gotcha: if we later enable Cilium with tunneling, adjust MTU (e.g., 8951 for jumbo) to prevent packet fragmentation. For now we'll stick with aws-vpc-cni.
maria: Tagging: add `kubernetes.io/cluster/prod-euc2=owned` and proper `k8s.io/role/elb` tags on public subnets.
infra-bot: quota-status: ENI limit 120 for eu-central-2; pending EIP increase.
aj: Security groups: Node SG must allow intra-SG all TCP for kubelet & metrics, 10250 TCP from control plane, and NodePort range if we need it. Lock down SSH.
devon: kube-proxy: stick with iptables mode for stability on our AMIs. IPVS sometimes requires kernel modules that are flaky on custom images.
samir: After nodes report Ready, confirm `kubectl describe node <node> | grep -i nvidia` shows allocatable `nvidia.com/gpu`. Then run NCCL allreduce smoke for multi-GPU health check.
maria: Autoscaling: set cluster-autoscaler annotations for ASG or set Karpenter Provisioner if we go that route. For spot, set mixed-instance-policy if using ASG to diversify.

```
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
metadata:
 name: prod-euc2

nodeGroups:
 - name: gpu-spot

```

aj: Pod networking: watch out for IP exhaustion on p4d if maxPods default high. Consider `maxPods` override per nodegroup or change packing to reduce pod count per node.

title: Scheduled service account token refresh failing after Okta policy update — nightly model-evals jobs stopped
text:
Issue summary:
- On 2026-02-28 ~01:10 UTC, multiple nightly model-evals cron jobs (model-eval-pipeline) failed to start; investigation shows the service account refresh token used by the scheduler returned invalid_grant.

Impact:
- Nightly evaluation and validation runs did not complete for ~6 hours (primary impact: model quality dashboards stale; secondary: delayed nightly cost reports).
- Approximately 12 scheduled jobs in prod us-east failed and retried until exhaustion.

Environment:
- Production cluster (k8s), us-east region.
- Scheduler: kubernetes CronJob invoking eval-runner service which requests a refreshed access token from identity-broker via Okta refresh token flow.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) CronJob triggers eval-runner pod.
2) Eval-runner calls identity-broker /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token and service-account refresh token.
3) Identity-broker calls Okta token endpoint; Okta responds 400 invalid_grant and revokes refresh token.
4) Eval-runner fails and exits; scheduler marks job failed.

Observed behavior:
- Okta token endpoint returns HTTP 400 with body: {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"The refresh token is invalid or has been revoked"}.
- No prior token rotation event recorded in platform key-rotation logs.

Expected behavior:
- Service account refresh tokens used by scheduled jobs should remain valid for rotation window or be automatically rotated by our token broker without causing job failures.

Initial hypothesis:
- A recent Okta Conditional Access policy enforcement (device trust) was tightened and inadvertently targeted the OU or client used by service account tokens, triggering revocation of refresh tokens for non-interactive sessions.

Telemetry and logs (excerpt):
- identity-broker logs (2026-02-28T01:09:58Z): "refresh token exchange failed: invalid_grant, okta error: token revoked by policy"
- scheduler logs (job eval-20260228-01): "Failed to obtain access token, retry count 0, aborting"
- Okta audit (admin): policy change id=pol-2026-02-27-7 by admin.carol -> enforced device_trust=true for group '/Services/NonInteractive'

2026-02-28 02:18 - Support Intake (Aisha): Initial ticket created after alerting on 12 failed cron runs. Notified #infra-ops and #platform-auth.
2026-02-28 03:05 - Marco H.: Started triage. Confirmed identity-broker received 400 invalid_grant from Okta. Pulling Okta audit logs next.
2026-02-28 03:40 - Lina S. (SRE): Observed the same pattern on two other non-eval cronjobs (backup-prune, billing-usage). Possibly broad impact to non-interactive service accounts.
2026-02-28 04:05 - Marco H.: Found Okta admin change: policy pol-2026-02-27-7 enabled device_trust and applied to group '/Services/NonInteractive' at 2026-02-27T23:57Z. Reached out to Identity team to request rollback or exception.
2026-02-28 05:20 - Identity Team (J. O'Neil): Confirmed policy rollout targeted the wrong group due to matching rule. We are reverting the policy to prior state and will create an allowlist for machine identities. Revert scheduled at 05:45 UTC.
2026-02-28 06:00 - Marco H.: Revert applied. Running a full retry of queued cron jobs. 10/12 jobs completed successfully after revert; 2 require manual rerun due to retry exhaustion—requeued.
2026-03-01 09:30 - Platform Eng (R. Gupta): Proposing permanent mitigation: migrate cron jobs to use Client Credentials flow (OAuth2.0) with rotation via Vault-issued JWTs and remove dependency on long-lived refresh tokens tied to interactive Okta policies.
2026-03-02 14:12 - Marco H.: Implemented emergency workaround doc and scheduled follow-up epic to migrate eval-runner to new token-broker flow. Assigned owners and timeline in linked Confluence.
2026-03-02 16:00 - Aisha P.: Customer-facing alert not required (internal-only). Closing impact window. Keeping ticket open until migration is complete.

Okta audit proves root cause: policy pol-2026-02-27-7 incorrectly matched '/Services/NonInteractive' and revoked refresh tokens for that group.
identity-broker treats Okta invalid_grant as non-retriable and fails job; this is expected but we should handle targeted policy revocations more gracefully (circuit-breaker + alerting to identity team).
Token rotation metadata shows last successful rotation for service-account 'svc-eval-runner' at 2026-02-20; no scheduled rotation in last week. Revocation was external (policy), not expired token.
We observed collateral failures in backup-prune and billing-usage cronjobs confirming policy scope was broad.

[identity-broker][2026-02-28T01:09:58Z] ERROR token_exchange.go:124 - refresh exchange failed for svc-eval-runner: okta response 400 invalid_grant (token revoked by policy)
[okta-audit][2026-02-27T23:57:12Z] ADMIN admin.carol - updated policy pol-2026-02-27-7 target: /Services/NonInteractive - device_trust=true
[scheduler][2026-02-28T01:10:03Z] cronjob eval-20260228-01 failed: unable to authenticate: refresh failed

Identity team reverted the policy at 2026-02-28T05:45 UTC which restored token refresh for affected service accounts. Two jobs that exhausted retries were manually requeued and completed. Temporary exception created for '/Services/NonInteractive' until permanent fix is live.

Short-term: Policy revert and allowlist for machine identities applied (completed).
Mid-term: Implement client-credentials-based broker for cron jobs and migrate eval-runner and other cron consumers.
Long-term: Add automated pre-deploy policy impact check and alerting when a policy targets groups with service-account clients. Add test coverage for non-interactive OU matching.
Owners: Identity team (lead J. O'Neil) for policy rules; Platform Eng (R. Gupta) for token migration; SRE (Lina S.) for runbook updates.

Create an epic to migrate all cron-based services to Client Credentials flow - owner: R. Gupta - due 2026-04-15
Add an alert rule for identity-broker 400 invalid_grant spikes mapped to service-account clients - owner: Lina S. - due 2026-03-07
Update runbook 'Service Account Token Failures' with Okta policy checks and rollback playbook - owner: Aisha P. - due 2026-03-05

title: PicoPrompt Labs
author: Alexei Ramos
text:
Inbound SMB lead from community tweet + self-serve signup. Founder (Jae Park) signed up, started with free tier and flipped to paid card after 2 days of traffic spikes. Primary ask: reduce per-month token spend — choppy notes below.

- Business: micro-SaaS for developer-facing in-editor help (VSCode extension) + small hosted web console. 12 engineers, heavy read/write of chat completions and embedding lookups for code search.
- Current setup: calling model via hosted API (trial), single GPT-like model, no caching, naive prompts. Token cost increasing fast after user growth (2k DAU -> 10k queries/day).
- Targets: 100-200ms median latency for chat completions (acceptable), 50ms-100ms for embedding retrieval pipeline, cost-sensitive: want 30-50% reduction in monthly model spend.
- Requirements: public cloud only, no VPC yet, wants SOC2 evidence and audit logs for future procurement. No on-prem.
- Technical asks from founder: 
 * "How do we batch without hurting perceived latency?"
 * "Can prefix caching reduce cost for our most common prompts?"
 * "Do you offer token usage auditing or prompt-compression guidance? We want a one-page plan."
- POC idea discussed: 7-day token audit of current traffic + sample config showing batching windows (e.g., 20-50ms batching for background tasks; immediate passthrough for interactive flows) + prefix/KV caching on repeated instruction prompts. Provide suggested prompt compression (system->instruction condensation) and sample savings estimate.
- AE notes: self-serve signup -> upgraded to paid card on 2026-03-02; trial volume peaked 2026-03-03. Founder receptive to short POC. Prefers async comms (email + Fireflies recap).
- Pricing negotiations: likely start month-to-month, convert to committed Dedicated only if traffic > 2M tokens/day (unlikely in 12 months).
- Quote from Jae: "We need a practical plan — show us how to cut our $/user in half without wrecking latency."
- Internal action items: assign POC template from SMB-hosted playbook, run quick eval with Redwood Optimize heuristics, collect 5 example high-volume prompts from their log (request sent).

Notes feel shorthand; follow-ups: schedule 30m technical deep-dive (SE + founder) after audit completes.

title: SLO Sentinel: Prefetch Routing and Graded Circuit Breakers for Multi-Region Requests
author: Asha Patel
text:
Problem: We see recurring SLO drift during regional capacity pressure and cold-KV-cache misses. Current geo-steering only reroutes after failures or gross latency spikes; this causes user-facing p99 regressions and noisy fallback loops. Goal: introduce an SLO-driven controller (SLO Sentinel) that (1) predicts imminent latency risk, (2) prefetches/warms KV cache and minimal model state in candidate regions, and (3) enforces graded circuit breakers and capacity-aware steering to avoid cascading failures while preserving high-priority traffic.

Design summary:
- SLO Sentinel: a central controller that ingests region-level telemetry (p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, capacity tokens) and computes a risk score per region using an EWMA trend + short-term derivative.
- Prefetch routing: when a region's risk score exceeds a warmup threshold, the controller triggers targeted prefetch ops to warm KV caches and small model kernels in the target region (prefetch budget controlled per-customer and globally). Prefetch uses an async lightweight path and applies only to routes with high recent locality.
- Graded circuit breakers (three bands):
 * Green (OK): normal steering by latency-weighted preference.
 * Yellow (degraded): soft-shed non-critical routes (batch jobs, non-PLG traffic) and divert new requests to nearby healthy regions; keep existing sessions sticky for a grace window.
 * Red (severe): open circuit for non-essential traffic; enforce strict geo-pin relax + route to fallback model variant (quantized/smaller) for critical sessions.
- Capacity-aware steering: instead of naive ejection, each request consumes a token from per-region capacity escrow. The routing decision is token-aware: prefer regions with headroom. A background allocator replenishes tokens based on autoscaler signals and a hysteresis window.

Key thresholds and SLOs (proposed):
- Interactive SLO: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 400ms global for hosted tier.
- Yellow trigger: region p99 > 350ms for 30s OR 70% GPU queue depth sustained for 60s.
- Red trigger: region p99 > 700ms for 15s OR >90% capacity tokens consumed.
- Prefetch budget: limit to 5% of traffic-equivalent warmups per region per minute; configurable per-customer.

Telemetry and metrics to add:
- region_risk_score (EWMA + derivative), prefetch_count, prefetch_success_rate, circuit_level{green,yellow,red}, capacity_tokens_total/consumed, headroom_estimate, route_latency_{p50,p95,p99} by route/model/region.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement controller and minimal hooks in runtime (prefetch API + token escrow) behind feature flag.
2) Internal canary: enable for infra test tenant in us-west-2 only (1% of prod traffic). Monitor SLOs, prefetch cost, and false positive warmups for 1 week.
3) Gradually expand to non-critical customers globally (10% traffic), then to all hosted API with opt-out.
4) For Dedicated customers, expose circuit-level controls and prefetch budgets as config in Console.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Prefetching reduces p99 but increases bandwidth and GPU cycles; cost must be guarded with budgets and per-customer limits.
- Over-eager prefetching could amplify thrash; we mitigate with derivative-based risk scoring and cooldowns.
- Token escrow adds complexity to routing; failure modes include token desync — plan includes reconciliation and fail-open paths.

Open implementation tasks:
- Add prefetch endpoints to runtime and a lightweight prewarm DAG (ENG tasks).
- Implement SLO Sentinel controller and scoring library.
- Telemetry: Grafana panels and alerts for circuit transitions and prefetch anomalies.
- Console UI: expose per-customer prefetch budget and circuit-level overrides.

Acceptance criteria:
- No regression on baseline SLOs in control regions.
- p99 improvement >=15% in simulated partial-capacity events in canary.
- Prefetch cost < 10% incremental infra cost in canary.
- Clear dashboards and alerts; on-call runbook updated.

2026-02-16 - Asha: Initial proposal posted; requested feedback from runtime and observability. Noted need for token escrow design (@Miguel) and prefetch API contract.
2026-02-20 - Miguel: Prototype of risk score function complete. Using EWMA(60s) + slope multiplier. Observability hooks added to the tracer. Shared synthetic test harness for partial capacity tests.
2026-02-28 - Priya (Product): Reviewed thresholds. Suggested lowering yellow trigger from 400ms->350ms for earlier soft-shed. Also asked for explicit controls per-tier (hosted vs dedicated).
2026-03-03 - Infra (review): Raised concern about prefetch causing inter-region egress spikes. Action: implement egress budget guard and metric to track cross-region warmup bytes.
2026-03-07 - Miguel: Created PR #5128 for controller skeleton and runtime prefetch API. CI tests failing on token reconciliation edgecase; assigned to eng-sre to investigate.
2026-03-09 - QA: End-to-end test plan added (load profiles simulating 30% capacity loss), test harness passed for green->yellow transition. Next: run long-tail tests for 48h.
2026-03-10 - Asha: Merged design doc into Confluence and routing spec updated. Plan to enable internal canary next week under feature flag.
2026-03-10 - Blocker: quota for cross-region warmups at cloud provider reached; infra ticket raised (ENG-304211).

title: Provisioning script fails on systems with legacy locale collation (NFKD) causing device-enroll and imaging stall
text:
Issue summary:
Provisioning helper script (setup_local_policies.sh) exits with non-zero when system locale uses legacy Unicode collation normalization (NFKD) or certain non-default LC_CTYPE/LC_COLLATE values. This stops the imaging task sequence mid-run and prevents Intune check-in/enrollment on a subset of repaired devices.

Impact:
- ~8 machines in the last two depot batches failed imaging and never completed Intune enrollment; users received a partially provisioned workstation (local accounts only, no corp certs).
- Blocks fast-redeploy for depot repair queue; increases turnaround time.

Environment:
- Affected devices repros on prod imaging pool in us-east.
- OS: Windows 11 22H2 corporate image (with latest platform patches as of 2026-03-01)
- Provisioning artifact: provisioning-scripts v2026.02.28 (bash + PowerShell wrapper)
- Managed via SCCM task sequence that runs setup_local_policies.sh late in the image.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Boot a test device (Dell Latitude 7440) into SCCM task sequence in the us-east imaging pool.
2) Set system locale environment to one of the affected collations (example repro used: LC_COLLATE="fi_FI@collation=NFKD" exported in cmd before running the script).
3) Allow task sequence to reach the provisioning-scripts step.
4) Observe that setup_local_policies.sh aborts with an encoding/collation exception and the task sequence halts.

Observed logs (excerpt):
- C:\Windows\Temp\provisioning\setup_local_policies.log:
 [2026-03-09 14:07:02] INFO: starting local policy setup
 [2026-03-09 14:07:03] ERROR: fatal: string normalization failed when writing registry key: "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\\SOFTWARE\\Redwood\\Provision"
 [2026-03-09 14:07:03] ERROR: exit code 1
- SCCM smsts.log shows task sequence step 'Run Command Line' returning 1 and aborting sequence.

Hypothesis and root cause (initial):
- The helper script uses Python 3.9 subprocess invocation and writes UTF-8 strings to the Windows registry using a small C# helper compiled during the build. Under certain LC_COLLATE/LC_CTYPE values the runtime performs Unicode normalization (NFKD) on strings and strips combining characters; combined with our registry write helper's unsupported normalization mode this results in an exception thrown by the helper (System.ArgumentException: Invalid character in registry value).
- This only triggers when a depot-repair process re-applies device-specific locale settings prior to provisioning (we see this on repaired devices that retain OEM locale overrides).

Temporary workaround applied:
- Imaging team added a wrapper to forcibly set LANG and LC_COLLATE to en_US.UTF-8 before running the provisioning step in the task sequence. This is in place for the current depot batch and prevents the failure.

Next steps / planned fix:
- Engineering (Provisioning) to update provisioning-scripts to sanitize locale inputs and coerce strings to NFC normalization before passing to the registry helper. Also update the C# registry writer to accept NormalizationForm variants. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-scripts/pull/412
- Imaging ops to roll the temporary LANG/LC_COLLATE wrapper into the standard task sequence until the patch is deployed.
- Confirm fleet-wide by running a small canary set of 20 repaired devices with the patch and removing wrapper after two successful batches.

Owner: Miguel Torres (Provisioning lead)
Estimated ETA for PR review & QA: 2026-03-16

Boot a device into SCCM task sequence in us-east imaging pool
Set system locale to a legacy collation variant (example: LC_COLLATE=\"fi_FI@collation=NFKD\") before provisioning step
Allow sequence to reach provisioning-scripts and observe failure

- 2026-03-10 09:20: initial report from depot engineer (see comment below).
- 2026-03-10 10:05: duplicated on Lenovo test device.
- Reproduced reliably by setting LC_COLLATE in PowerShell and running the provisioning script under an elevated cmd shell.
- Confirmed exception originates from Registry write helper when passed composed characters.
- Confirmed wrapper fix prevents failures for current imaging batches.

2026-03-10 09:18 - Jordan Mills (Depot): Noticed 3/30 repaired laptops failed at provisioning step - all had OEM locale overrides. Dumped setup_local_policies.log and attaching to ticket.
2026-03-10 11:02 - Aisha Patel (IT Support): Assigned to Miguel for provisioning-engineering investigation. Added tag 'locale' and moved to In Progress.
2026-03-10 13:40 - Miguel Torres (Provisioning): Reproduced on Dell + Lenovo. Hypothesis: registry writer rejects certain Unicode normalization. Will raise PR to sanitize strings and extend registry helper behavior.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Imaging Ops (Claire Huang): Applied LANG/LC_COLLATE wrapper to active task sequence (tsid: TS-2026-111). Current batch (15 devices) now completes imaging. Suggest keeping wrapper until fix is merged.
2026-03-11 16:45 - Miguel Torres (Provisioning): PR #412 opened to coercion-to-NFC and guard rails added to C# helper. Requesting code review from SRE for potential side effects on internationalization.
Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioning-scripts/pull/412

Set LANG and LC_COLLATE to en_US.UTF-8 (or remove OEM locale overrides) in SCCM task sequence before invoking provisioning scripts. Imaging Ops to keep wrapper until patch deployed.

Update provisioning-scripts to normalize strings to NFC before registry writes and harden the C# registry helper to accept multiple normalization forms. Add unit tests for legacy collation inputs. Roll patch through canary imaging pool and remove LANG wrapper after verification.
