title: SLI contract friction and cross-team learning sprint retrospective (Nov 2024)
author: Priya Natarajan
text:
Overview:

This retrospective captures the outcomes from the two-week cross-team learning sprint (Nov 4–18, 2024) that emerged after multiple small but persistent SLI contract breaks across platform components. The goal of the sprint was to: (1) surface where SLI definitions and alert contracts diverged between teams, (2) produce concrete dashboard and alert changes that reduce noisy page wakes, and (3) update operator-facing runbooks to speed diagnosis.

Summary of findings:
- Multiple teams (allocator, prefetch-controller, router, kv-prefix-cache) had subtly different interpretations of the same SLIs (e.g., "token_cost_per_request" vs "token_cost_per_user_request").
- Alerts were firing during legitimate transient load patterns due to brittle burn-rate thresholds and missing context panels (tenant, region, model_variant).
- Operators lacked a compact decision canvas that maps an alert to the minimal triage checklist; this increased mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) by ~14 minutes for the incidents observed.

Why this matters:
- Repeated noisy wakes increase cognitive load on oncall, leading to escalation fatigue and slower response for customer-facing failures.
- Misaligned SLI semantics drive inefficient mitigations (over-provisioning, unnecessary rollbacks, customer-impacting throttles).

Sprint timeline and scope:
1) Nov 4–6: Discovery interviews with allocator, prefetch, routing, and telemetry teams.
2) Nov 7–10: Correlate alert history with token-cost and latency SLI graphs (historical window: Sep–Nov).
3) Nov 11–14: Implement dashboard prototypes and adjusted alert rules in staging.
4) Nov 15–18: Run operator tabletop exercises and collect feedback; finalize runbook edits.

Incident examples (representative) and impact:
- Incident A (2024-10-29): Prefetch-controller alert group fired repeatedly for burn_rate > 1.2 for 5m. Root cause: transient multi-tenant warmup spike combined with an alert that ignored tenant priority. Oncall paid ~28 minutes of hands-on investigation before demoting to monitoring-only.
- Incident B (2024-10-31): Router p95 foreground latency SLI breached (threshold 450ms p95). Alerts lacked model_variant context and routed to infra team instead of serving runtime — added 22 minutes of routing handoffs.

Root causes and evidence:
- SLI naming drift: teams stored token-cost metrics under different labels (token_cost.count, token_cost.request_sum, token_cost.user_request_sum). This caused dashboards and composite SLIs to disagree. Evidence: PromQL queries used by allocator (token_cost.request_sum / requests_total) vs prefetch (token_cost.count / user_requests_total).
- Alert burn-rate sensitivity: burn-rate thresholds tuned for sustained regressions (targeting 30–60 minute degradations) but applied at 5–10 minute windows by several legacy alerts.
- Missing contextual dimensions: most alerts did not include tenant_id, model_variant, or region tags, making it hard for oncall to determine blast radius.

Key dashboards and alert changes (deployed to staging Nov 12, promoted Nov 16):
- New composite panel: "Token cost per effective request (by tenant)"
 - Query (PromQL example): sum by (tenant_id) (increase(token_cost.request_sum[10m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (increase(requests_total[10m]))
 - Visualization: stacked area + table with top 25 tenants by cost delta.
- Alert rule: token-cost-gradual-burn
 - Old: burn_rate(token_cost.request_sum[5m]) > 1.2 for 3m
 - New: burn_rate(token_cost.request_sum[15m]) > 1.15 AND topk(3, increase(token_cost.request_sum[15m])) / increase(requests_total[15m]) > 1.1 for same tenants
 - Rationale: extend window to filter transients; only page when top tenants drive the change.
- Latency alert adjustment: router-p95-deg-guard
 - Old: p95(router_latency_ms)>450ms for 10m
 - New: p95(router_latency_ms{model_variant!="fallback"})>500ms for 15m AND increase(error_count[15m])>5
 - Rationale: ignore known fallback variants and require traffic-impact signal.

Runbook and operator-facing updates:
- New triage canvas (one-page) added to runbooks: "S3: Signal, Scope, Stabilize"
 - Signal: confirm metric delta and check burn-rate over 5/15/60m.
 - Scope: narrow to tenant/model_variant/region using dashboard drilldowns.
 - Stabilize: apply blue-green routing to target model_variant or enact tenant soft-quota; avoid immediate global rollbacks.
- Runbook snippet (shell helpers and queries):
 1) Quick tenant list: curl -s http://ops-api/internal/top-tenants?window=15m | jq '.'
 2) Prefetch warmset health: kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=prefetch-controller -o wide
 3) Check KV prefix shard states: redis-cli -h kv-prefix-cache-01 INFO keyspace || redis-cli -h kv-prefix-cache-02 INFO keyspace

Operator tabletop outcomes and metrics:
- MTTA reduced from baseline 16.4m -> 9.8m in staged exercises (avg across 6 scenarios).
- False-positive page rate for token-cost alerts dropped ~62% in staging over two weeks.
- Operator confidence score (survey, n=12) increased from 2.6 -> 3.8 /5 for triage clarity.

Decisions and governance changes (approved Nov 18):
- All SLI definitions exposed in the shared telemetry repo must include canonical metric name, recommended aggregation window, primary dimensions (tenant_id, region, model_variant), and owner. (See Appendix: SLI metadata template).
- New "SLI change request" flow: small SLI changes may be approved by two owners (observability + affected service). Larger semantic changes require a 5-day notice and cross-team review.

Action item list (owners and ETA):
1) Telemetry team: publish canonical SLI metadata for token-cost, router-latency, and kv-read-latency. (Owner: Marta Gómez; ETA: 2024-12-05)
2) Prefetch team: add tenant-level breakdown panels to public platform dashboard. (Owner: Arjun Patel; ETA: 2024-12-12)
3) Observability: update alert library with burn-rate templates and parameterized examples. (Owner: Ethan Rodriguez; ETA: 2024-12-08)
4) Oncall: adopt the "S3 triage canvas" into weekly runbook training. (Owner: Liam Chen; ETA: 2025-01-15)
5) Platform product: document cost-aware routing fallback policies in the public operator guide. (Owner: Priya Natarajan; ETA: 2024-12-22)

Roadmap/Follow-ups for Q1 2025:
- Q1 sprint: SLI metadata registry (service: telemetry-sli-registry) with an API and a UI for cross-team discovery.
- Dashboards: template library of compact triage dashboards that can be instantiated per model_variant and tenant slice.
- Automated page suppression: short-term generator to gate burn-rate paging if the top-k metric contributor is a pre-approved maintenance window.

Lessons learned (concrete):
- Small differences in metric naming cause outsized operational friction; invest in canonicalization early.
- Burn-rate is an effective early-warning signal but must be tuned with windowing and contributor context to avoid noise.
- Operator training and a one-page triage canvas materially reduce cognitive load and response time.

Appendix A — SLI metadata template (example):
| field | example | notes |
|---|---|---|
| canonical_name | token_cost.per_request | metric namespace used in Prometheus |
| promql_example | sum by (tenant_id) (increase(token_cost.request_sum[15m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (increase(requests_total[15m])) | recommended query to compute SLI |
| aggregation_window | 15m | default window for burn-rate and smoothing |
| primary_dimensions | [tenant_id, model_variant, region] | required tags for dashboards/alerts |
| owner | team/telemetry | team responsible for correctness and migration |

Appendix B — Example alert YAML (operational template):
---
alert: token-cost-gradual-burn-template
expr: |
 sum by (tenant_id) (increase(token_cost.request_sum[15m])) / sum by (tenant_id) (increase(requests_total[15m])) > 1.1
for: 15m
labels:
 severity: warning
 team: platform-telemetry
annotations:
 summary: "Token cost per request rising for tenant {{ $labels.tenant_id }}"
 runbook: "https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-platform/runbooks/s3-triage-canvas"

Appendix C — Owners matrix (compact):
- Telemetry: Marta Gómez (owner), Ethan Rodriguez (support)
- Prefetch: Arjun Patel (owner), Mei Lin (support)
- Router: Samir Desai (owner), Liam Chen (support)
- Oncall: Liam Chen (owner), Priya Natarajan (support)

Contact and next steps:
- We will track progress in the eng-platform quarterly board (epic: SLI-contract-cleanup-Q1-2025).
- If you are an owner listed above, please add weekly 15-minute sync items to your calendar through Dec 2024 and post progress updates to the #platform-telemetry Slack channel.

Document history:
- Drafted: 2024-11-18 by Priya Natarajan
- Reviewed and updated after operator tabletop: 2024-11-20 (Ethan Rodriguez, Marta Gómez)
- Promoted to published: 2025-01-20 after completing staging validations and initial runbook adoption exercises.

title: Intent-anchored profile merger and staged changelog sifter
author: Ava Martinez
text:
Summary: introduce an intent-aware profile merger that consolidates incoming model performance profiles while preserving workload-specific signals (chat, completion, embeddings, reranking). Add a staged changelog sifter that ranks suggested release notes by estimated customer impact and signal provenance so release drafts are concise and prioritised.

Motivation: onboarding spikes frequently carry redundant or conflicting profile entries when the same model is ingested from multiple sources (community uploads, model zoo mirrors, vendor bundles). Naive merges collapse metrics and lose workload-specific tails (e.g. long-chat latency vs short-completion p50). This causes regressions for customers who rely on per-intent profiles. The changelog authoring process also floods release notes with low-importance deltas; we need a lightweight ranking to surface high-impact items.

What this PR changes:
- Add an intent-anchor data model (profile.intent_tags and profile.anchor_fingerprint) and merger logic that performs a two-phase merge: 1) intent stratification to group subprofiles by intent vectors, 2) anchor-preserving aggregation that keeps representative exemplars for each intent and computes merged distributional stats (p10/p50/p90, tokenized latency histograms).
- Implement a staged changelog sifter service which consumes profile deltas and emits ranked changelog fragments with provenance (source repo, onboarding agent, telemetry sample size). The sifter uses heuristics: weight by relative regression magnitude, sample volume, user-visible metric (e.g. quality drop on canonical prompt sets), and per-intent footprint.
- Introduce a lightweight provenance token (profile.provenance_token) used by the console to trace release snippets back to source commits and telemetry slices.
- Add migration path: an on-disk transformer that detects legacy profile documents and backfills intent tags using a heuristic classifier based on prompt distribution hash.

Checklist: 
- [x] Intent-anchor model and schema changes
- [x] Merger algorithm + unit tests
- [x] Changelog sifter + integration tests
- [x] Migration transformer and data-sanity checks
- [x] Console slice to show provenance token and ranked changelog preview
- [x] Docs: registry onboarding guide + changelog authoring notes

Commits (high-level):
- Add intent anchor schema and migration helper
- Implement two-phase merger (intent stratify + anchor-preserve agg)
- Changelog sifter service and ranking heuristics
- Console UI hook for provenance token and ranked preview
- Tests: unit + integration + e2e for representative scenarios

Files changed (high level):
- src/registry/schema/profile.ts -> adds intent_tags, anchor_fingerprint, provenance_token
- src/registry/merger/intent_merger.py -> core algorithm (new)
- src/registry/changelog/sifter_service.go -> ranking and output formatter (new)
- migrations/2026-02-intent-backfill.py -> legacy profile detector/backfiller
- web/console/src/components/ChangelogPreview.tsx -> UI hook for ranked preview
- docs/registry/onboarding.md -> docs + examples

Testing and CI: all unit and integration tests were run in CI. Initial CI run failed on a flaky e2e (console snapshot mismatch) — fixed by updating stable snapshot generation; rerun passed. CI summary: build & unit tests passed, integration tests passed, e2e passed on rerun.

Backward compatibility: the schema change is additive. Migration included; operator-run migration recommended for large registries. No breaking API changes expected for consumers of profile read endpoints.

Related Linear/JIRA: Linear: ENG-4823, ENG-5631, PM-211
Related PRs: small console tweak PR #547981 (console preview styles)

Merge: squash and merge. Merge commit includes the migration script and a short runbook note for operators.

Notes for reviewers: focus on intent stratification heuristics in intent_merger.py and the ranking weights in sifter_service.go — both are intentionally conservative and parameterized for rollout. The migration backfill is purposely non-destructive (writes into profile.intent_tags only when confidence > 0.85).

Liam O'Connor (reviewer): The stratification looks good but we should guard the p90 merge when sample_count < 100 to avoid noisy spikes.
Ava Martinez (author): Good catch — added a min_sample_count parameter (default 100) and a fallback to median-based imputation when sample_count is low.
Priya Shah (reviewer): Can the provenance_token be translated to a console deep link? Would help debugging.
Ava Martinez (author): Yes — added a console route /profiles/:id/provenance that maps token -> telemetry slice. Added unit tests for the link resolver.
Marco Rossi (reviewer): The changelog ranking weights need an opt-out; SRE may not want automated notes surfaced for infra-only deltas.
Ava Martinez (author): Added a allowlist and an opt-out label (changelog:manual) so infra-only deltas are filtered from automatic suggestions.

- Add intent-anchored profile merging to preserve per-workload signals
- Introduce staged changelog sifter that ranks release snippets by estimated customer impact
- Migration tool to backfill intent tags for legacy profiles

Run migrations/2026-02-intent-backfill.py in dry-run mode first and validate a sample of profiles for accuracy. For registries >10M profiles, run backfill on a rolling window and monitor profile-read latency during migration.

text:

- Company: B2B SaaS building in-app chat assistant embedded in their product (developer tools + customer support).

title: Add Chrome extension RAG quickstart with offline index and synced tool-calls
author: Priya Menon
text:
Summary: This PR introduces a new quickstart that demonstrates embedding-based RAG inside a Chrome extension with (1) an offline IndexedDB-backed indexer, (2) a small background worker that batches and syncs new documents to an optional Redwood Private sync endpoint, and (3) an example of reliably forwarding tool-calls (open-in-tab, search, and external API proxies) from the extension to a trusted tool runtime.

Motivation: We have many requests for lighter-weight client-side RAG experiences and reproducible examples for browser-based agents that need to work offline or with intermittent connectivity. This quickstart shows one pragmatic pattern: keep a local index for immediate recall/latency, emit telemetry and async sync to server-side storage for durability and cross-device replay, and handle tool-calls via a verified background channel to avoid leaking user tokens.

What changed (high level):
- New quickstart folder quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/ with README, manifest, background worker, popup UI, IndexedDB indexer, and a small local test harness.
- New docs page docs/contributing/extension-guidelines.md that outlines security considerations for browser extensions (token handling, CSP, permission scoping).
- Add a lightweight node helper server in quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/proxy-server/ (optional) that demonstrates a recommended pattern to host tool runtimes behind a short-lived signed session token.
- Tests and Playwright-based smoke runner in .github/workflows/quickstart-chrome.yml to validate build and basic flows in CI.

Usage and testing:
- Follow quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/README.md to load the unpacked extension in Chrome (dev). The README includes a one-command flow to run the local proxy and seed an index.
- The extension exposes an "index page" where you can drag text/files to index; it will generate embeddings (using your Redwood API key from environment) and store them in IndexedDB.
- When offline, the extension searches the local index and renders results. When connectivity is restored, it batches unsynced items and posts to the proxy server or Redwood Private sync endpoint.
- Tool-calls (for example, openUrl and runSearch) are routed to the background worker which will either run locally (open tab) or forward to the proxy-server endpoint using a short-lived ephemeral token.

Security notes:
- The quickstart README and docs/contributing/extension-guidelines.md explicitly show how to avoid storing long-lived API keys in localStorage and how to delegate to a backend to sign ephemeral tokens.
- We recommend using Redwood Private for production sync; the proxy server is intentionally minimal and documented as NOT production-ready.

Commits (summary):
- add: initial chrome extension quickstart scaffold (manifest, popup, background)
- feat: add indexeddb indexer + embeddings integration
- feat: add node proxy-server example and signing helper
- docs: extension security + CONTRIBUTING notes
- ci: add Playwright smoke check and workflow
- test: add local integration test (index/search cycle)

Files changed (high level):
- quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/README.md
- quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/manifest.json
- quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/src/background.ts
- quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/src/popup.tsx
- quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/src/indexer/indexeddb.ts
- quickstarts/chrome-extension-rag/proxy-server/server.js
- docs/contributing/extension-guidelines.md
- .github/workflows/quickstart-chrome.yml

Small illustrative snippet (from indexeddb.ts) included inline in README for clarity: const db = await openDB('redwood-extension', 1); await db.put('docs', { id: id, text: text, embedding: embedding });

Review conversation (selected):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer): "Nice pattern — can we avoid storing embeddings in plain IndexedDB if the extension is marked for public distribution? Suggest an opt-in encrypted store and clarify in docs."
- Priya Menon (author): "Agreed; added a section in extension-guidelines.md describing an optional IndexedDB encryption shim using Web Crypto API and a template for prompting the user to enable encryption."
- Xiaoyu Zhang (reviewer): "CI smoke run failed on first attempt due to Playwright connecting to headless Chrome in CI image. Recommend switching to ubuntu-latest and adding xvfb in workflow."
- Priya: "Fixed: updated workflow to use the official Playwright action which sets up the browsers; also added retries for the smoke check."
- Marisol Reyes (reviewer): "Can you add a quick note about long-running syncs causing battery drain and a recommended throttle?"
- Priya: "Added throttle settings to README and the proxy-server example (batch size 32, delay 5s default)."

CI status and runs:

- Checks: build: pass; smoke-playwright: pass; lint: pass; docs-linkcheck: pass

Merge notes:

- Merge method: squash (squash merge commit used).

Related: Linear ENG-1432 (browser quickstarts initiative), PM-321 (quickstarts backlog).

Account summary: enterprise streaming/media company. Heavy live-event traffic patterns - large bursts during finals and premieres.

POC kickoff (2025-11-05) - SE Daniel ran baseline tests with 8-GPU cluster; simulated bursts up to 25k req/min. Observed p50 ~60ms, p95 drift to 320ms under sudden ramp.
Technical findings (POC report 2025-12-08): partial queueing under cold-start burst, KV cache warmup mitigates tail but not instantaneous spikes. Recommended: pre-warmed burst nodes + autoscale buffer + aggressive batching config for embeddings pipeline.
EdgeWave engineering notes: concerned about queue growth during 5-10 minute surges (premieres). Target SLO: p95 <= 200ms for captions and personalization. Cost sensitivity: wants <35% increase over current vendor run-rate.
Security review in parallel - requested SOC2/ISO snippets, encryption at rest keys, KMS integration. Security team flagged data residency for EMEA and stricter retention controls. Delivery stalled while legal & security negotiate contract language.
Competitive pressure: EdgeWave engaged OpenAI-managed endpoints and Anthropic for evaluation. Sales reported that competitor promised simpler autoscaling and a flexible burst promise; procurement cited pricing + perceived risk as deciding factors.
Commercial timeline: procurement halted by company-wide hiring freeze and budget reforecast (2026 Q1). AE notes 'budget freeze across several platform projects - deprioritized until Q3).'

Internal assessment: technical fit is borderline but solvable - recommended changes were infrastructure pre-warm, larger burst pool, and tuned batching. Main non-technical blockers (budget, champion) caused stall. Likely lost to competitor who promised turnkey burst scaling.
Next suggested actions (internal): attempt executive sponsor intro, offer a one-off pre-warmed burst pilot for critical events at discounted rate, provide a formal queueing mitigation design doc (SLA + warm pools + circuit-breakers).

- Confirm whether EdgeWave will accept periodic health-check reports while in freeze - awaiting reply.

title: people-ops
text:
Noor A: Hey folks 914 quick benefits/payroll q after my first week: I'm auto-enrolled in the 401k but want to confirm match details, vesting schedule, and whether contributions are prorated if you start mid-pay-period (I started 2025-06-10). Also trying to choose between HSA vs Health FSA 6b8 9fe any guidance? Lastly, do company holidays get pro-rated for new hires or do we get the full allotment?

Jules (People Ops): Welcome Noor! :wave: Short answers: 401k match = company matches 100% of the first 3% deferred then 50% of the next 2% (so max 4% total). Vesting is on a 3-year graded schedule (33% after year 1, 66% after year 2, fully vested after year 3). Contributions are taken each pay period; if you started mid-pay-period your first paycheck will reflect only the pay and deductions for the days worked in that period (prorated).

Noor A: Thanks. How do I change my deferral % and where do I see the match posting?

Benefits Admin: Change deferral in the 401k vendor portal (link in Workday > Benefits > Retirement). Match posts each quarter to your 401k account and you'll see a company contribution line in the vendor statement. If you want us to walk through the portal, DM and we can do a screenshare.

Payroll Bot: Payroll notes: Redwood runs biweekly payroll on Fridays. For a mid-period start the gross/withholdings are proportional to days/hours. Employer 401k match is an after-pay-period posting by Finance (quarterly), not a per-pay-period line item.

Noor A: HSA vs FSA practical differences? I have a high-deductible plan.

Benefits Admin: If you have a qualifying HDHP, HSA is generally better long-term: funds roll over year-to-year, employer contributions (if any) and your pre-tax contributions grow tax-free, and it's portable. FSA is use-it-or-lose-it (some limited carryover). For 2025 HSA max employee+employer = $4,600 (family), FSA health limit = $3,050. Also check if Redwood contributes to HSA (some teams get a small employer seed).

Noor A: Does enrollment into HSA lock me for the year?

Jules (People Ops): You can only change elections mid-year with a qualifying life event. Open enrollment next November otherwise.

Noor A: About holidays 384 are new hires entitled to the full set of holidays immediately?

Sam F: Holidays: Redwood publishes 10 company holidays + 1 floating. For payroll, non-exempt employees get paid holidays if employed on the holiday date. We don't prorate the holiday count but if your start date is after a holiday you won't retroactively get it. For exempt staff, holiday pay is handled per policy in Workday > Time Off tab.

Noor A: One last thing 4dd I submitted an expense for desk lamp/reimb last Tue under "newhire-setup" in Expensify. Any ETA?

Jules (People Ops): Reimbursements are reviewed within 3 business days by People Ops, then Finance issues payment on the next AP run (Tues/Thu). If amount > $500 we need manager approval which can add a day. If you paste the Expensify link/ID here we'll flag it.

Noor A: Cool thanks! Appreciate the clarity :clap:

title: SlateBridge RepoAnalytics
author: Eleanor Brooks
text:
Background: SlateBridge builds repository analytics and developer productivity tooling for large engineering orgs (mono-repo customers).
Primary ask: enterprise-grade code search + RAG layer for internal engineering docs and code. Embeddings + reranking pipeline must handle large corpus (initial target: 10M embeddings, long-term 50M+).
Latency/throughput targets: 95th perc token/response latency target < 200ms for first-pass embedding similarity (p99 < 500ms end-to-end with reranker), tail latency critical (developer-facing hotpaths).
Cost target: aiming for <$0.002 per query (embedding search + rerank amortized) for >500k queries/day; heavy emphasis on batching & cache reuse to reach unit economics.
Indexing requirements: frequent re-indexing of repos (delta-index every 30m, full index nightly). Need fast incremental embeddings pipeline and invalidation hooks when PRs merge.
Retrieval architecture preference: hybrid approach — bi-encoder for large-scale ANN retrieval + cross-encoder reranker for top-K (configurable topK 10-50). Must support on-the-fly rerank fallback when precision drops.
Model constraints: prefer open models (quantized) for private infra but open to Redwood-verified suggestions; need deterministic outputs for legal tracking of suggestions in code-assistant flows.
Security/compliance: SSO via SAML (Okta), audit trails for query / token-level metadata, KMS integration for key separation, data residency: US-only for initial deployment, potential EU expansion in 2027.
Deployment preference: Private control plane in customer VPC or on-prem appliance for legal/regulatory customers. Must support peered VPC endpoints and private Egress to internal artifact stores.
POC summary: initial 2-week POC to validate throughput, rerank quality, and cost projections. POC dataset: 12 repos (~120GB raw), expected ~11M chunked embeddings after sliding-window tokenization.
Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-01-18: Intro + scoping call (Fireflies ff_20260118_3b9c2a). AE/SE covered indexing cadence and security must-haves.
- 2026-01-25: Architecture workshop with infra team; discussed VPC peering and private control plane options. SE created preliminary network diagram.
- 2026-02-02: Customer shared sample data + SAML metadata (drive link). Requested cost model scenarios for 3 query volumes (50k, 500k, 2M q/day).
- 2026-02-08: SE ran local microbenchmarks on quantized bi-encoder candidate (internal note: 2–3x speedup on A100 q4_0 configs). Shared preliminary numbers via Gmail thread gt_20260202_repo-indexing-POC.
- 2026-02-12: Security review kickoff; customer requested SOC2 scope and audit log retention matrix. Redwood provided security FAQ link (drive).
- 2026-02-13: Internal Redwood ops aligning on dedicated GPU pool sizing for POC; SE opened infra tickets RR-4122 (indexing infra) and RR-4189 (reranker latency tuning).
Sales/PS notes: customer values observability — token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency dashboards are a big win. They asked about auto-batching behavior and KV cache reuse for repeated code search queries (repeated developer queries to same repo paths).
Technical open questions (customer):
- How does Redwood handle delta embedding updates with minimal re-embedding? Looking for change-detection hooks and chunk-level idempotent upserts.
- Can reranker run on CPU for cost savings with acceptable latency for topK=20? Need benchmark on c5a/EPYC family.
- What are consistent snapshot semantics for queries when a nightly full reindex is running? Need to avoid flapping results for in-flight user sessions.
Sales quotes / customer language from call: 'We cannot accept >5% dev-facing flakiness during working hours' and 'We need predictable unit economics — pull the levers to hit <$0.002/query'.
Next steps (short):
- SE to deliver 24h scheduled indexing run plan and resource request (target by 2026-02-18).
- Customer to share SAML metadata and legal DPA redlines (expected 2026-02-21).
- Redwood to run reranker-on-CPU microbenchmarks and provide three cost/latency options (CPU-only, hybrid CPU+GPU, GPU-only) by 2026-02-20.
Potential blockers: Legal/DPA negotiation window, customer firewall rules delaying VPC peering, sample data anonymization for POC if required by privacy team.
Recommended Redwood playbook items: prioritize a small dedicated GPU pool for cross-encoder POC; enable prefix/KV caching and aggressive batching for developer interactive workloads; provide a detailed data residency / audit log PDF to accelerate legal review.
Stated win condition for POC: demonstrate sub-200ms p95 initial retrieval (bi-encoder ANN) and sub-500ms end-to-end p99 with reranker for 95% of traffic, with cost model below target at 500k q/day scenario.

title: Add runbook links + remediation hints to unit economics alert payloads
author: Aisha Bello
text:
Context

We’ve had a couple of "unknown page / where do I start" escalations when the Unit Economics pipeline alerts fire (freshness/completeness/anomaly checks). The alerts today include the alert name, labels, and a few raw counters, but they don’t provide:
- a direct runbook link
- the most common remediation steps
- a pointer to validation queries / backfill command entrypoints

This PR updates the alert payloads emitted by the economics pipeline (and the alert templates used by the internal notifier) to include runbook links + short remediation hints so first responders can take action without context switching.

What’s in this PR

1) Alert payload schema enhancements
- Adds optional fields to the canonical alert payload:
 - runbook_url (string)
 - remediation (short bullet-like string; kept intentionally brief)
 - dashboard_url (string; used when we have a Grafana panel / Console deep link)
- Keeps backward compatibility: existing consumers ignore unknown fields; no required field changes.

2) Runbook mapping + link hygiene
- Introduces a small mapping table keyed by alert_id (NOT by free-form alert name) to avoid drift as names/labels evolve.
- Uses stable internal go-links for Confluence/Grafana targets where possible (prevents Slack history from rotting when pages move).
- Adds a default fallback for unknown alerts: runbook_url points to the index page for the Unit Economics oncall guide.

3) Alert renderer / Slack + PagerDuty payloads
- Slack: appends:
 - "Runbook: <link>"
 - "First steps: …"
 - "Dashboards: <link>" (when present)
- PagerDuty: includes the same fields in custom_details so the oncaller sees it in the incident UI.

4) Tests
- Unit tests cover:
 - mapping lookup behavior
 - fallback behavior
 - rendering of Slack blocks + PD custom_details
 - ensures remediation stays < 280 chars (avoids noisy payloads / truncation)

Examples

Before (Slack)
- "unit-econ.hourly_aggregation.missing_hours" + labels

After (Slack)
- unit-econ.hourly_aggregation.missing_hours
- Runbook: https://go.redwood/runbook-unit-econ-missing-hours
- First steps: check ingestion lag; validate hourly completeness view; if lagged, re-run aggregation for affected hours; if dropped rows, check region mapping + null handling
- Dashboards: https://go.redwood/grafana-unit-econ-pipeline

Rollout / risk

- This is safe to roll out broadly: schema change is additive.
- Scoped initially to Unit Economics alerts only.
- If we discover any formatting regressions, we can disable via the notifier config flag `include_runbook_links` (defaults ON for unit-econ routes).

References
- ENG-8435 (Create runbook pages and link from alerts)
- ENG-8429 (Completeness/anomaly checks)
- Related: pr-19383-add-data-quality-checks-for-economics-pipeline.json (introduces the checks that fire these alerts)

Screenshots
- Included in internal review (Slack block formatting) — see "Checks" artifacts in CI run.

Allison Grant (review): Can we ensure the runbook link won’t break if Confluence pages move? Prefer go-links over raw confluence URLs.
Aisha Bello (author): Yep — updated mapping to use go-links for all entries. Added a test to reject confluence URLs unless explicitly whitelisted (only the index page uses a direct confluence short URL right now).
Sean Gallagher (review): Where does `alert_id` come from? Want to make sure it’s stable and not derived from a label that can change.
Aisha Bello (author): `alert_id` is a constant in the check definitions (same place we define alert_name). This PR adds an assertion that alert_id is present and matches /^[a-z0-9_.-]+$/; also updated the check registry so IDs are shared between the alert emitter and the mapping table.
Caleb Johnson (review): The remediation field looks like it could get long. Are we risking truncation in PagerDuty custom_details / Slack blocks?
Aisha Bello (author): Added a 280-char guardrail (unit test) and trimmed a couple of verbose steps. For anything longer we link to the runbook section "Common remediation".
Mei Lin (review): For missing hours alerts, can we include a direct link to the validation query snippet? That’s usually step 1.
Aisha Bello (author): Added `dashboard_url` for the pipeline completeness panel, and the runbook section has the exact SQL. Keeping the Slack message light per SRE guidance but it should be 1 click now.
Allison Grant (approval): LGTM after go-link change + length guardrail.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Additive schema change looks safe; thanks for scoping to unit-econ routes.
